title: Differentiated mosquito adaptive strategies underlie regional dominance of three ECSA sub-lineages in chikungunya virus
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has emerged as a rapidly expanding global health threat and has been reported in 119 countries and territories, with recent outbreaks across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype has increasingly predominated in multiple regions, yet the molecular basis of its competitive advantage remains unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that three ECSA sub-lineages—ECSA-IOL, ECSA-2.1, and ECSA-2.2—have independently evolved distinct vector-associated evolutionary patterns that underlie their divergent geographic dominance. Using comparative phylogenomic analyses of complete CHIKV genomes and selection pressure analyses (RELAX/BUSTED/Contrast-FEL), we found that ECSA-2.1 showed intensified selection on structural-protein genes and accumulated substitutions previously associated with Aedes aegypti , explaining its rapid displacement of the Asian genotype across the Americas. In contrast, ECSA-IOL underwent adaptation strategy switching from Aedes albopictus to Ae. aegypti , maintaining its dominance across South and Southeast Asia, while ECSA-2.2 convergently acquired Ae. albopictus adaptation with additional envelope protein mutations, suggesting enhanced adaptive potential. Genome-wide analysis revealed lineage-characteristic and convergent substitutions, providing molecular signatures associated with ECSA competitive advantage. These findings suggest vector niche partitioning as an important driver of CHIKV global expansion dynamics, with potential implications for outbreak forecasting, vector control prioritization, and the design of broadly protective vaccines.

abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)已成为迅速扩展的全球健康威胁,并已在119个国家和地区报告,近期在亚洲、欧洲和美洲出现了暴发。东/中/南部非洲(ECSA)基因型在多个地区日益占据主导地位,但其竞争优势的分子基础仍未明确。在这里,我们证明了三种ECSA亚谱系——ECSA-IOL、ECSA-2.1和ECSA-2.2——已独立进化出与媒介相关的不同进化模式,这些模式解释了它们在地理上的不同优势。通过比较全基因组系统发育分析和选择压力分析(RELAX/BUSTED/Contrast-FEL),我们发现ECSA-2.1在结构蛋白基因上表现出增强的选择压力,并积累了此前与Aedes aegypti相关的替代,这解释了其在美洲迅速取代亚洲基因型的现象。相比之下,ECSA-IOL从Aedes albopictus向Ae. aegypti切换了适应策略,维持了其在南亚和东南亚的优势,而ECSA-2.2则通过获得Ae. albopictus适应性以及额外的包膜蛋白突变,表现出趋同的适应性获得,表明其具有增强的适应潜力。对基因组的全基因组分析揭示了谱系特异性及趋同的替代,提供了与ECSA竞争优势相关的分子特征。这些发现表明,媒介的生态位分化是CHIKV全球扩展动态的重要驱动因素,可能对暴发的预测、媒介的控制优先级以及设计广泛保护性的疫苗具有潜在影响。

title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.
abstract: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the application of nanopore sequencing in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomics, addressing the need for rapid, portable, and accurate methods to track viral diversity and evolution during outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the principles and application of nanopore sequencing for Chikungunya virus, examining its use in clinical and vector samples to recover complete genomes and monitor viral spread.
analysis.methods: Nanopore sequencing was used to directly sequence RNA and DNA by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling real-time, single-molecule analysis of Chikungunya virus genomes without the need for culture.
analysis.main_results: The method demonstrated the ability to rapidly recover full viral genomes from clinical and vector samples, facilitating real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread during outbreaks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as a significant advancement in pathogen surveillance, particularly for resource-limited settings, where nanopore sequencing provides a flexible and powerful tool for monitoring Chikungunya virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective genomic surveillance strategies for Chikungunya virus, enhancing outbreak response and epidemic preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges challenges in basecalling and error correction but highlights robust quality control pipelines that ensure reliable results, supporting a moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the application of nanopore sequencing in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomics, emphasizing its advantages in real-time, portable, and long-read analysis. The research highlights how nanopore sequencing enables rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from clinical and vector samples, facilitating real-time tracking of viral diversity and spread. The authors interpret these findings as a significant advancement in pathogen surveillance, particularly for resource-limited settings, where the method offers flexibility and power. The study notes challenges in basecalling and error correction but underscores the reliability of quality control pipelines. These results have implications for improving genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness for CHIKV. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the acknowledged limitations in the sequencing process, though the method's potential is well-supported by prior experiences with other pathogens.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)基因组学中的应用,以应对在疫情期间快速、便携和准确追踪病毒多样性及传播的迫切需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究聚焦于纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒中的原理与应用,考察其在临床和环境样本中用于恢复完整病毒基因组和监测病毒传播的使用情况。
elements_zh.methods: 纳米孔测序通过测量核酸穿过纳米级孔时的离子电流变化,直接对RNA和DNA进行测序,从而实现对基孔肯雅病毒基因组的实时、单分子分析,无需依赖培养。
elements_zh.main_results: 该方法展示了从临床和环境样本中快速恢复完整病毒基因组的能力,有助于在疫情期间实时追踪病毒多样性、传播及扩散。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为病原体监测领域的重要进展,特别是在资源有限的环境中,纳米孔测序提供了一种灵活且强大的工具,用于基孔肯雅病毒的监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为基孔肯雅病毒的更有效监测策略的制定提供依据,从而增强疫情响应和疫情应对能力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究承认在碱基调用和错误校正方面存在挑战,但强调了稳健的质量控制流程,确保了可靠的结果,支持了中等程度的证据可信度。

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as a significant advancement in pathogen surveillance, particularly for resource-limited settings, where nanopore sequencing provides a flexible and powerful tool for monitoring Chikungunya virus.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective genomic surveillance strategies for Chikungunya virus, enhancing outbreak response and epidemic preparedness.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges challenges in basecalling and error correction but highlights robust quality control pipelines that ensure reliable results, supporting a moderate confidence in the evidence.

title_zh: 纳米孔测序用于基孔肯雅病毒:原理与应用。
source_body_en: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)基因组学中的应用,以应对在疫情期间快速、便携和准确追踪病毒多样性及传播的迫切需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究聚焦于纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒中的原理与应用,考察其在临床和环境样本中用于恢复完整病毒基因组和监测病毒传播的使用情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 纳米孔测序通过测量核酸穿过纳米级孔时的离子电流变化,直接对RNA和DNA进行测序,从而实现对基孔肯雅病毒基因组的实时、单分子分析,无需依赖培养。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该方法展示了从临床和环境样本中快速恢复完整病毒基因组的能力,有助于在疫情期间实时追踪病毒多样性、传播及扩散。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为病原体监测领域的重要进展,特别是在资源有限的环境中,纳米孔测序提供了一种灵活且强大的工具,用于基孔肯雅病毒的监测。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为基孔肯雅病毒的更有效监测策略的制定提供依据,从而增强疫情响应和疫情应对能力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究承认在碱基调用和错误校正方面存在挑战,但强调了稳健的质量控制流程,确保了可靠的结果,支持了中等程度的证据可信度。

title: Overview of Chikungunya Virus Epidemiology, Biology, and Pathogenesis.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)概述、生物学及系统发育
source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.

title: Successful use of a Janus-kinase (JAK) inhibitor in chronic chikungunya arthritis refractory to conventional synthetic DMARDs: a case report
abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic chikungunya arthritis is a debilitating post-viral inflammatory condition that clinically mimics rheumatoid arthritis and often requires long-term treatment with disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. Treatment options are limited when conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs are not tolerated or lose efficacy. We report the case of a 50-year-old Brazilian woman with serologically confirmed chikungunya virus infection who developed chronic chikungunya arthritis with a rheumatoid arthritis–like phenotype. Following an acute febrile illness accompanied by rash and negative dengue serology, she was initially managed with symptomatic analgesics, followed by prednisone and hydroxychloroquine. Despite this treatment, the disease activity score in 28 joints calculated with C-reactive protein was elevated at 6.78. Methotrexate was introduced but was discontinued after three weeks due to drug-induced pneumonitis. She later failed leflunomide therapy after 12 months, with a score of 4.33. Baricitinib (4 mg/day), a Janus kinase 1 and 2 inhibitor, was then initiated, resulting in marked clinical and laboratory improvement: the disease activity score decreased to 1.90 over one year, C-reactive protein normalised and the erythrocyte sedimentation rate declined progressively, and morning stiffness resolved, with no infectious complications. This case suggests that Janus kinase inhibition may be a therapeutic option for selected patients with chronic chikungunya arthritis refractory to conventional treatment.

title: Protocol for Detecting and Sequencing Chikungunya Virus from Field-Collected Mosquitoes.
abstract: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.

Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.

abstract_zh: 蚊媒疾病是公共卫生领域的重要挑战,尤其是在热带地区,环境条件可能有利于蚊虫媒介的繁殖和传播。因此,对蚊虫种群中基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)进行早期和准确的检测,可以成为有效监测流行变异株和识别新病毒引入的宝贵工具。鉴于在野外捕获的蚊虫中检测蚊媒病毒的挑战,我们描述了一种集成的工作流程,用于CHIKV的分子检测和全基因组测序。该方案包括使用基于珠子的机械破碎仪对蚊虫进行匀浆,使用TRIzol试剂进行RNA提取(略有修改),使用CHIKV特异性RT-qPCR进行分子筛选,以及全基因组扩增后在Illumina平台上进行测序。尽管该方案针对单个蚊虫进行了优化,但仍能获得高质量的RNA,适用于虫媒监测和基因组分析。由于该方案能够从蚊虫样本中回收完整的CHIKV 基因组,因此可以作为基因组流行病学研究的基础,实现对病毒多样性及谱系动态的监测,并有助于早期发现新兴变异株,从而支持在流行和高风险地区及时、有针对性的公共卫生干预措施。

title: Tactical Paralysis: The Interplay Between Chikungunya Virus and Host Mitochondrial Dynamics in Immune Evasion and Metabolic Remodeling
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an expanding alphavirus causing acute febrile illness, yet its most debilitating signature remains the refractory chronic arthralgia persisting for months or years. While traditional paradigms focused on viral-mediated host shutoff, emerging evidence points to a more insidious orchestrated sabotage within the joint niche. This review deconstructs the tactical paralysis of host mitochondrial dynamics driven by CHIKV. We delineate how specific viral components (nsP2, TF, and 6K) act as molecular wedges or post-translational modifiers that hijack host fission/fusion machinery (Drp1/Mfn2), driving the mitochondrial network into compulsive fragmentation. Crucially, this morphological collapse operates as a double-edged sword: in the acute phase, it disrupts the MAVS signalosome to mute the type I interferon response; in the chronic phase, it cascades into a profound immunometabolic rewiring within the synovial microenvironment. In synovial macrophages, mitochondrial fragmentation ruptures the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, causing succinate accumulation that epigenetically locks cells into a persistent, pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype, establishing a destructive "metabolic memory." Concurrently, in fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS), retrograde signaling from mitochondrial ROS and cytosolic mtDNA leakage prompts a pseudo-malignant transformation, accelerating extracellular matrix degradation via MMP-13 and RANKL hyperactivation. By integrating these dimensions, we provide a unified framework for CHIKV chronicity and propose targeted mitochondrial quality control as a high-value therapeutic frontier to break post-viral arthropathy.
journal: International Journal of Biology and Health

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in causing chronic arthralgia through its manipulation of host mitochondrial dynamics. The study highlights how viral components such as nsP2, TF, and 6K interfere with mitochondrial fission and fusion processes, leading to fragmentation. This fragmentation serves dual purposes: it suppresses the type I interferon response during the acute phase and initiates immunometabolic rewiring in the chronic phase. The review identifies specific mechanisms, including the disruption of the TCA cycle in macrophages and the activation of MMP-13 and RANKL in fibroblast-like synoviocytes, which contribute to persistent inflammation and extracellular matrix degradation. The findings suggest that targeting mitochondrial quality control could offer a promising therapeutic approach for managing post-viral arthropathy. The review emphasizes the need for further research into these mechanisms to develop effective interventions.

Concurrently, in fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS), retrograde signaling from mitochondrial ROS and cytosolic mtDNA leakage prompts a pseudo-malignant transformation, accelerating extracellular matrix degradation via MMP-13 and RANKL hyperactivation. By integrating these dimensions, we provide a unified framework for CHIKV chronicity and propose targeted mitochondrial quality control as a high-value therapeutic frontier to break post-viral arthropathy.

title: Workflow for Long-Read Amplicon Sequencing of Chikungunya Virus Using Oxford Nanopore Technology.
abstract: This protocol provides a comprehensive, step-by-step workflow for whole-genome sequencing of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) using an amplicon-based strategy optimized for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platforms. The procedure includes detailed instructions for sample handling, viral RNA extraction, quality control, cDNA synthesis, multiplex PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and primary bioinformatic processing. The protocol is designed to maximize reproducibility across laboratories and is suitable for genomic surveillance applications, including outbreak investigation and molecular epidemiology, even when working with low-to-moderate viral loads.

title: Optimized Amplicon Strategy for Long-Read Sequencing of the Chikungunya Virus Genome.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

title: Assessing the Vector Competence for Chikungunya Virus in Mosquitoes.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a human pathogenic, mosquito-borne virus (arbovirus), which is causing epidemic outbreaks among human populations in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South- and Central America including the Caribbean. The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory. In this chapter, we describe how to prepare Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for the infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV. We also describe quantitative and qualitative viral detection assays in mosquitoes based on plaque assays and the amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.

title: Chikungunya Virus Infection of Monocytes Generates a Persistent Macrophage Reservoir That Promotes IFN-π/IL-27–STAT1- and NF-κB–Driven Chronic Arthritis
abstract: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection causes acute febrile illness that frequently progresses to chronic arthralgia. Although monocytes are CHIKV targets, whether viral exposure drives their differentiation into macrophages to sustain persistent inflammation remains incompletely understood. To address this, we integrated transcriptomic profiling of pediatric CHIKV patients during acute and convalescent phases, in vitro differentiation of primary human monocytes into macrophages under CHIKV infection, and single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) of joint-associated macrophages from an immunocompetent mouse model of chronic CHIKV arthritis at 28 days post-infection. In acute patients, we observed a marked upregulation of monocyte/macrophage markers alongside robust, IFN-dependent JAK-STAT signaling. In vitro , CHIKV-infected monocytes differentiated into persistently infected macrophages (MDM-CHIKV) that closely aligned with an M1-polarized transcriptional profile. These cells exhibited STAT1/NF-κB-dependent inflammation, ISG induction, and enhanced antigen presentation capacity. Author Summary Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a mosquito-borne pathogen that causes acute fever and, in a substantial proportion of patients, progresses to chronic, debilitating joint pain that can last for months or even years. The mechanisms by which the virus establishes this persistent arthritic disease remain poorly understood, and effective treatments for chronic CHIKV arthritis are lacking. In this study, we investigated whether CHIKV infection of monocytes, immune cells that circulate in the blood, actively drives their transformation into macrophages, a cell type that resides in tissues and plays a central role in inflammation. By analyzing blood samples from children with acute and convalescent CHIKV disease, we found strong signs that monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation is actively occurring during natural infection. Using an in vitro model, we showed that CHIKV-infected monocytes differentiate into macrophages that become persistently infected, carrying the virus for extended periods. These virus-exposed macrophages adopt a mixed activation state, combining features of classical pro-inflammatory (M1) and regulatory (M2) macrophages. Notably, they produce a cytokine called IFN-π/IL-27, which drives chronic inflammation through a specific signaling pathway, while also showing enhanced capacity to activate T cells, trigger complement cascades, and mount strong oxidative responses upon encountering immune complexes, features that may explain the waxing and waning joint symptoms seen in patients. To confirm these findings in a living system, we analyzed joint tissues from a mouse model of chronic CHIKV arthritis using single-cell technology. We discovered that a specific subset of joint-resident macrophages serves as the primary viral reservoir, actively replicating the virus and producing IFN-π/IL-27 and other inflammatory molecules that perpetuate joint inflammation and damage. Collectively, our work reveals that CHIKV hijacks the normal differentiation process of monocytes to create a long-lived, virus-harboring macrophage population that fuels chronic joint inflammation. We identify the IFN-π/IL-27 signaling pathway, complement activation, and antibody-driven macrophage responses as key drivers of disease. These findings open new avenues for therapeutic intervention, suggesting that targeting these pathways could alleviate chronic arthritis in patients suffering from long-term CHIKV disease.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解单核细胞的 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 感染是否会促使其分化为巨噬细胞,从而维持慢性炎症和关节炎。这解决了了解慢性 CHIKV 关节炎背后机制的知识差距,这是一个重大的公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究结合了儿科 CHIKV 患者样本、原代人单核细胞的体外分化,以及来自慢性 CHIKV 关节炎免疫功能正常小鼠模型的关节相关巨噬细胞的单细胞 RNA 测序。
elements_zh.methods: 从 CHIKV 患者中分离单核细胞并在体外感染以分化为巨噬细胞。进行转录组分析和单细胞 RNA 测序来分析基因表达模式并确定关键信号通路。
elements_zh.main_results: CHIKV 感染的单核细胞分化为持续感染的巨噬细胞 (MDM-CHIKV),其表现出混合的 M1/M2 激活状态、强大的 JAK-STAT 信号传导和增强的抗原呈递能力。单细胞 RNA 测序证实,小鼠模型中的关节巨噬细胞也表现出 IFN-π/IL-27 表达升高和其他炎症特征。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究表明,CHIKV 感染会驱动单核细胞向巨噬细胞分化为持续感染的、M1 偏向的混合表型,该表型充当病毒 储存宿主,并通过 IFN-π/IL-27 信号传导和增强的 免疫应答 加剧慢性关节炎。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了靶向 IFN-π/IL-27 信号通路、补体激活和抗体驱动的巨噬细胞反应对于慢性 CHIKV 关节炎治疗干预的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于使用动物模型且缺乏直接的人类干预试验而受到限制。由于该研究的观察性质以及需要在人类受试者中进一步验证,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 摘要 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 感染会导致急性发热性疾病,并经常进展为慢性 关节痛。尽管单核细胞是 CHIKV 的靶标,但病毒暴露是否会促使其分化为巨噬细胞以维持持续的炎症仍不完全清楚。为了解决这个问题,我们整合了儿科 CHIKV 患者在急性期和恢复期的转录组学分析、CHIKV 感染下原代人单核细胞体外分化为巨噬细胞,以及感染后 28 天对慢性 CHIKV 关节炎免疫活性小鼠模型的关节相关巨噬细胞的单细胞 RNA 测序 (scRNA-seq)。在急性患者中,我们观察到单核细胞/巨噬细胞标记物显着上调,同时存在强健的 IFN 依赖性 JAK-STAT 信号传导。在体外,CHIKV 感染的单核细胞分化为持续感染的巨噬细胞 (MDM-CHIKV),其与 M1 极化转录谱密切相关。这些细胞表现出 STAT1/NF-κB 依赖性炎症、ISG 诱导和增强的抗原呈递能力。值得注意的是,MDM-CHIKV 独特地产生 IFN-π/IL-27,揭示了一个替代的非规范轴,其中尽管不存在经典的 I 型 IFN,JAK-STAT 激活仍然持续存在。从功能上讲,MDM-CHIKV 在吸收免疫复合物后表现出增强的呼吸爆发,这表明 FcγR 介导的病理学以及补体激活和 T 细胞刺激能力。然而,在 TLR4 攻击后,这些细胞通过 IL-10 和 TGF-β 保留了部分调节反应;这种混合免疫表型为复发性 关节痛 提供了潜在的机制解释。此外,小鼠关节的 scRNA-seq 证实,持续的 CHIKV 复制仅限于类似于 MDM-CHIKV 的独特巨噬细胞子集,从而将这些细胞确定为主要的体内病毒 储存宿主。与我们的人类研究结果相似,关节相关的小鼠巨噬细胞亚群表现出 IFN-π / IL-27 表达升高以及强大的 NF-κB/STAT1 依赖性炎症特征(Tnf、Il1β、Il6、Ccl2、Ccl5、Cxcl9、Cxcl10、Cxcl1–3 和/或 Ptgs2),强调了它们在维持慢性关节炎中的关键作用。总的来说,我们的研究结果表明,CHIKV 主动驱动单核细胞向巨噬细胞分化为持续感染的、M1 偏向的混合表型,充当病毒 储存宿主 并加剧促关节炎炎症。因此,巨噬细胞重编程、非经典 IFN-π/IL-27-STAT1 轴、FcγR 介导的吞噬作用和补体激活成为中心致病节点和缓解慢性 CHIKV 后关节病的有希望的治疗靶点。作者摘要 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 是一种由蚊子传播的病原体,会引起急性发烧,并且在相当一部分患者中会发展为慢性、衰弱性关节疼痛,可持续数月甚至数年。该病毒引起这种持续性关节炎疾病的机制仍知之甚少,并且缺乏治疗慢性 CHIKV 关节炎的有效 治疗。在这项研究中,我们研究了单核细胞(血液中循环的免疫细胞)的 CHIKV 感染是否会主动驱动其转化为巨噬细胞(一种驻留在组织中并在炎症中发挥核心作用的细胞类型)。通过分析患有急性和恢复期 CHIKV 疾病的儿童的血液样本,我们发现了强烈的迹象,表明自然感染期间单核细胞向巨噬细胞的分化正在活跃发生。使用体外模型,我们发现 CHIKV 感染的单核细胞分化为巨噬细胞,巨噬细胞会持续感染,并长时间携带病毒。这些暴露于病毒的巨噬细胞采用混合激活状态,结合了经典促炎性(M1)和调节性(M2)巨噬细胞的特征。值得注意的是,它们产生一种名为 IFN-π/IL-27 的细胞因子,通过特定的信号通路驱动慢性炎症,同时还表现出增强的激活 T 细胞、触发补体级联反应以及在遇到免疫复合物时产生强烈氧化反应的能力,这些特征可以解释患者所见的关节症状的变化。为了在生命系统中证实这些发现,我们使用单细胞技术分析了慢性 CHIKV 关节炎小鼠模型的关节组织。我们发现关节驻留巨噬细胞的特定子集充当主要病毒 储存宿主,积极复制病毒并产生 IFN-π/IL-27 和其他炎症分子,使关节炎症和损伤永久化。总的来说,我们的工作表明,CHIKV 劫持了单核细胞的正常分化过程,以产生长寿的、携带病毒的巨噬细胞群,从而加剧慢性关节炎症。我们确定 IFN-π/IL-27 信号通路、补体激活和抗体驱动的巨噬细胞反应是疾病的关键驱动因素。这些发现为治疗干预开辟了新途径,表明针对这些途径可以缓解患有长期 CHIKV 疾病的患者的慢性关节炎。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解单核细胞的 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 感染是否会促使其分化为巨噬细胞,从而维持慢性炎症和关节炎。这解决了了解慢性 CHIKV 关节炎背后机制的知识差距,这是一个重大的公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究结合了儿科 CHIKV 患者样本、原代人单核细胞的体外分化,以及来自慢性 CHIKV 关节炎免疫功能正常小鼠模型的关节相关巨噬细胞的单细胞 RNA 测序。
analysis_zh.methods: 从 CHIKV 患者中分离单核细胞并在体外感染以分化为巨噬细胞。进行转录组分析和单细胞 RNA 测序来分析基因表达模式并确定关键信号通路。
analysis_zh.main_results: CHIKV 感染的单核细胞分化为持续感染的巨噬细胞 (MDM-CHIKV),其表现出混合的 M1/M2 激活状态、强大的 JAK-STAT 信号传导和增强的抗原呈递能力。单细胞 RNA 测序证实,小鼠模型中的关节巨噬细胞也表现出 IFN-π/IL-27 表达升高和其他炎症特征。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究表明,CHIKV 感染会驱动单核细胞向巨噬细胞分化为持续感染的、M1 偏向的混合表型,该表型充当病毒 储存宿主,并通过 IFN-π/IL-27 信号传导和增强的 免疫应答 加剧慢性关节炎。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了靶向 IFN-π/IL-27 信号通路、补体激活和抗体驱动的巨噬细胞反应对于慢性 CHIKV 关节炎治疗干预的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于使用动物模型且缺乏直接的人类干预试验而受到限制。由于该研究的观察性质以及需要在人类受试者中进一步验证,证据强度中等。

title: Surface Plasmon Resonance-Based Analysis of Ligand Binding Kinetics in Chikungunya Virus Drug Discovery.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

title: RT-RPA-Assisted CRISPR/Cas12a-Based Isothermal Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11-12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation.

title: Production of Viral Particles from a Chikungunya Virus Infectious Clone.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, which poses challenges for its study and genetic manipulation. Because direct mutagenesis of viral RNA genomes is technically impractical, reverse genetics systems are essential tools for investigating viral biology. To enable such approaches, infectious clones containing a full-length cDNA copy of the viral genome are constructed. The cDNA is positioned under the control of a bacteriophage RNA polymerase promoter, allowing commercial RNA polymerases to use the linearized plasmid as a template for the in vitro transcription of full-length viral genomic RNA (gRNA). Importantly, positive-sense viral genomes serve as mRNAs for the translation of viral proteins in a cellular environment, meaning that these transcripts contain all the information required to initiate viral replication. Following transfection into permissive cultured cells, viral proteins are expressed, enabling genome replication and, ultimately, the recovery of infectious particles from the cell supernatant. Here, we describe a detailed procedure for generating CHIKV particles through plasmid linearization, in vitro transcription, and subsequent RNA transfection.

title: Accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure to forecast chikungunya outbreaks in Reunion Island and Paraguay: a mathematical modelling study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heterogeneity in mosquito exposure at a fine spatial scale is well documented but often neglected in mathematical models of arbovirus transmission, particularly for real-time forecasting. We aimed to assess whether accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure improves the ability of transmission models to reproduce past chikungunya outbreaks and to forecast an ongoing outbreak in real time. METHODS: We extended an existing transmission model, originally developed to forecast dengue outbreaks in Reunion Island and incorporating seasonality, to include heterogeneity in mosquito exposure. We compared this model to versions assuming homogeneous exposure, evaluating their ability to reproduce the 2005-06 Reunion Island outbreak and the 2023 Paraguay Metropolitana subregion outbreak. We then used the heterogeneity model to forecast the 2025 Reunion Island outbreak in real time. abstract_zh: 背景:在细尺度空间上蚊虫暴露的异质性已被充分记录,但在基孔肯雅病毒的数学模型中往往被忽视,尤其是在实时预测方面。我们旨在评估是否考虑蚊虫暴露的异质性能够提高模型再现过去基孔肯雅热暴发的能力,并改善对当前暴发的实时预测。方法:我们扩展了一个现有的数学模型,该模型最初用于预测留尼汪岛的登革热暴发,并包含季节性因素,以纳入蚊虫暴露的异质性。我们将此模型与假设蚊虫暴露同质性的模型版本进行比较,评估其再现2005-06年留尼汪岛基孔肯雅热暴发和2023年巴拉圭Metropolitana子区域基孔肯雅热暴发的能力。随后,我们使用异质性模型对2025年留尼汪岛的基孔肯雅热暴发进行实时预测。结果:在细尺度空间上考虑蚊虫暴露的异质性对于准确再现2005-06年留尼汪岛的基孔肯雅热暴发至关重要。同质性模型要么高估了最终病例数(80% vs 观察到的38%),要么在干预后需要将基本再生数减少约50%,这在现实中是不合理的。从此次基孔肯雅热暴发中估计的异质性水平成功地转移到了Metropolitana子区域的暴发中,准确预测了疫情轨迹和最终病例数(异质性模型为约40%,同质性模型为约75%)。在相同假设下,异质性模型成功预测了2025年留尼汪岛基孔肯雅热暴发的峰值(约每周400次急诊就诊)和时间(4月),提前近两个月。暴发后的血清学调查显示,异质性模型低估了最终病例数(46·1% vs 观察到的61·6%),而同质性模型则高估了最终病例数(78·5%),这表明2025年的异质性可能低于2005-06年。解释与创新性:这些结果突显了在蚊虫暴露中考虑异质性如何提高基孔肯雅热暴发的预测能力。我们的方法在具有气候季节性的环境中表现出强大的预测性能,并为未来基孔肯雅热及其他蚊媒病毒的预测提供了前景。资助:欧盟;新兴传染病整合生物学卓越实验室计划;国家艾滋病、病毒性肝炎和新兴传染病研究所;国家研究署。局限性与证据强度:暴发后的血清学调查显示,异质性模型低估了最终病例数(46·1% vs 观察到的61·6%),而同质性模型则高估了最终病例数(78·5%),这表明2025年的异质性可能低于2005-06年。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 我们旨在评估在蚊虫暴露异质性方面进行调整是否能提高传播模型再现过去基孔肯雅热暴发的能力,并实时预测当前暴发暴发的能力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们扩展了一个现有的传播模型,该模型最初开发用于预测留尼汪岛的登革热暴发,并结合了季节性因素,以纳入蚊虫暴露的异质性。
analysis_zh.methods: 我们将该模型与假设同质暴露的版本进行了比较,评估其再现2005-06年留尼汪岛暴发和2023年巴拉圭大都会区子区域暴发的能力。
analysis_zh.main_results: 同质模型要么高估了最终的血清流行率(80% vs 38% 观察到的),要么需要在干预措施实施后将基本再生数减少约50%,这在现实中是不可行的。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果突显了在蚊虫暴露中纳入异质性如何提高基孔肯雅热暴发的预测能力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 资助:欧盟;新兴传染病整合生物学卓越实验室计划;国家艾滋病、病毒性肝炎和新兴传染病研究局;法国国家研究局。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 一项关于暴发的血清学调查表明,异质性模型低估了最终的血清流行率(46·1% vs 观察到的61·6%),而同质性模型则高估了最终的血清流行率(78·5%),这表明2025年的异质性可能比2005-06年更低。

title: Naked-Eye Visual Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Method for the Rapid Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) represents a significant global health threat due to its recent resurgence. This protocol highlights the use of capillary-modified visual loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) technology for the rapid detection of CHIKV. We employed Vero cells for virus propagation and utilized the MolPure Viral DNA/RNA Kit for nucleic acid extraction, successfully amplifying extracted viral RNA at 63°C for 25 min. The presence of CHIKV was indicated by a distinct yellowish-green color change, demonstrating the effectiveness and simplicity of this protocol. Our protocol underscores the potential of LAMP technology as a rapid diagnostic tool for CHIKV, enabling timely public health interventions.

analysis.summary_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) poses a growing global health threat, prompting the development of a rapid detection method. Researchers established an in vitro protocol using Vero cells to propagate CHIKV, extracted viral RNA with the MolPure kit, and performed loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) at 63 °C for 25 minutes. Detection relied on a distinct yellowish-green color change, confirming CHIKV presence and demonstrating the assay’s simplicity and effectiveness. The authors interpret this as a promising rapid diagnostic tool that could enable timely public health interventions. By offering a point-of-care, visual LAMP assay, the protocol has the potential to enhance CHIKV surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. No limitations or evidence strength assessments were reported in the abstract.

title: Plaque Reduction Neutralization Test Against Chikungunya Virus Using Liver Homogenate.
abstract: We adapted the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to detect chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates instead of serum. This approach enables serological investigation using tissues collected from animal carcasses as nonhuman primate ones, during arbovirus surveillance, expanding opportunities for CHIKV monitoring and strengthening epidemiological surveillance efforts.

title: In Silico Drug Design of Chikungunya Antivirals: Using Consensus Methods for Virtual Screening.
abstract: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅热 抗病毒药物 的计算机药物设计:使用共识方法进行虚拟筛选。
source_body_en: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

title: Expression and Purification of nsP2 Protease of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: The nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an essential cysteine protease involved in viral polyprotein processing and replication complex regulation. Biochemical and structural studies of nsP2 require the availability of highly pure and enzymatically active protein. In this chapter, we describe a straightforward protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain (nsP2pro) in Escherichia coli. The protein is expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions by immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.

title: Chikungunya Virus Infection in Paraffin-Embedded Tissue: Analysis of Histological Alterations and Viral Detection by Immunohistochemistry.
abstract: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. title: Assessing Chikungunya Virus Protease Activity and Pharmacological Inhibition Using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp Fluorogenic Peptide Substrate.
abstract: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.

title_zh: 使用 acc-CHIK 15 -dnp 荧光肽底物评估 基孔肯雅病毒 蛋白酶活性和药理抑制。
source_body_en: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.
abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 是一种蚊媒甲病毒,由于其快速传播且缺乏经批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法,对全球健康构成重大威胁。病毒非结构蛋白 2 蛋白酶 (nsP2p) 在加工病毒多蛋白以产生关键病毒酶方面发挥着关键作用,使其成为药物开发的有吸引力的目标。在本研究中,我们描述了重组 CHIKV nsP2 蛋白酶的表达和纯化,并建立了强大的荧光测定法,使用 acc-CHIK 15 -dnp 肽底物测量其酶活性。该测定能够实时监测蛋白水解裂解,并提供评估小分子抑制剂的平台。我们提出了大肠杆菌中蛋白质表达、亲和纯化和标签去除的优化条件,从而获得适合生化表征的高纯度 nsP2 蛋白酶。使用该系统,我们还提供了一个强大的方案来确定候选抑制剂的 IC50 值。这项工作为 CHIKV 蛋白酶抑制剂的高通量筛选提供了一种可重复的方法,有助于发现针对 基孔肯雅病毒 的潜在 抗病毒药物 化合物。

title: Quantification of Chikungunya Virus RNA by Real-Time RT-PCR Assay.
abstract: RT-qPCR is characterized by‌ high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, ‌enabling‌ rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. The real-time PCR system relies upon the measurement of a fluorescent reporter during PCR, in which the amount of emitted fluorescence is directly proportional to the amount of the PCR product in a reaction. Here, we describe the use of TaqMan® probe-based one-tube Real-time reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the detection and quantification of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) RNA.

The authors highlight the assay’s high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, which together enable rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. While the abstract outlines the assay’s design and the principle of fluorescence measurement proportional to PCR product, it does not provide details on study design, population, or quantitative performance data. The work represents a methodological advance in CHIKV diagnostics, but further data are required to assess its clinical and epidemiological utility.

title: Determination of Chikungunya Virus Infectious Titer Using Plaque Assays.
abstract: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

title: Automated Counting of Chikungunya Virus-Formed Plaques.
abstract: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 形成的斑块的自动计数。
source_body_en: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

title: A-083 Rapid screening for acute chikungunya virus infection using an interpretable machine learning model based on routine complete blood count parameters.
abstract: Abstract Background The 2025 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) outbreak in Foshan, China, highlighted an urgent need for rapid screening tools. Molecular diagnostics are constrained by time, cost, and availability. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model using routine complete blood count (CBC) parameters to identify patients at high risk of CHIKV infection. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 1,537 suspected CHIKV patients from two medical centers in Foshan. CBC and cell population data (CPD) were obtained using Mindray BC-7500 analyzers. CHIKV infection was confirmed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). After rigorous data preprocessing and feature selection using LASSO regression, four models Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and LightGBM (LGBM) were developed on a training set (n=1,132 from Center A) and evaluated on an internal test set (n=192) and an independent external test set (n=213 from Center B). Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and net benefit. Results In the external validation set, the LR model demonstrated superior and robust performance (AUC = 0.807, sensitivity = 88.0%, specificity = 65.0%, NPV = 93.0%), significantly outperforming the tree-based models. Decision curve analysis confirmed its clinical utility across a wide range of risk thresholds. SHAP analysis revealed that lower white blood cell count (WBC_N), lower lymphocyte percentage (Lym%), and increased neutrophil morphological heterogeneity (D_Neu_SSC_CV) were the strongest predictors, aligning with the established pathophysiology of CHIKV infection. Conclusion We developed an interpretable LR model based on CBC parameters that can effectively screen for acute CHIKV infection with high sensitivity and NPV. This model serves as a reliable, rapid, and cost-effective tool for patient triage during outbreaks, especially in resource-limited settings awaiting confirmatory PCR testing.

title_zh: A-083 使用基于常规全血细胞计数参数的可解释机器学习模型快速筛查急性 基孔肯雅病毒 感染。
source_body_en: Abstract Background The 2025 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) outbreak in Foshan, China, highlighted an urgent need for rapid screening tools. Molecular diagnostics are constrained by time, cost, and availability. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model using routine complete blood count (CBC) parameters to identify patients at high risk of CHIKV infection. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 1,537 suspected CHIKV patients from two medical centers in Foshan. CBC and cell population data (CPD) were obtained using Mindray BC-7500 analyzers. CHIKV infection was confirmed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). After rigorous data preprocessing and feature selection using LASSO regression, four models Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and LightGBM (LGBM) were developed on a training set (n=1,132 from Center A) and evaluated on an internal test set (n=192) and an independent external test set (n=213 from Center B). Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and net benefit. Results In the external validation set, the LR model demonstrated superior and robust performance (AUC = 0.807, sensitivity = 88.0%, specificity = 65.0%, NPV = 93.0%), significantly outperforming the tree-based models. Decision curve analysis confirmed its clinical utility across a wide range of risk thresholds. SHAP analysis revealed that lower white blood cell count (WBC_N), lower lymphocyte percentage (Lym%), and increased neutrophil morphological heterogeneity (D_Neu_SSC_CV) were the strongest predictors, aligning with the established pathophysiology of CHIKV infection. Conclusion We developed an interpretable LR model based on CBC parameters that can effectively screen for acute CHIKV infection with high sensitivity and NPV. This model serves as a reliable, rapid, and cost-effective tool for patient triage during outbreaks, especially in resource-limited settings awaiting confirmatory PCR testing.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 2025年在中国佛山发生的基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)疫情凸显了快速筛查工具的迫切需求。分子诊断方法受到时间、成本和可获得性的限制。本研究旨在利用常规的全血细胞计数(CBC)参数开发并验证一种可解释的机器学习模型,以识别CHIKV感染的高风险患者。方法 本研究回顾性分析了来自佛山两家医疗机构的1,537例疑似CHIKV患者的资料。使用迈瑞BC-7500分析仪获取全血细胞计数(CBC)和细胞群体数据(CPD)。通过逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)确认CHIKV感染。在进行严格的数据预处理和使用LASSO回归进行特征选择后,基于训练集(来自中心A的n=1,132例)开发了四个模型:逻辑回归(LR)、支持向量机(SVM)、随机森林(RF)和LightGBM(LGBM),并在内部测试集(n=192)和独立的外部测试集(来自中心B的n=213例)上进行评估。模型性能通过接收者操作特征曲线下的面积(AUC)、灵敏度、特异性和净效益进行评估。结果 在外部验证集中,LR模型表现出优越且稳定的性能(AUC = 0.807,灵敏度 = 88.0%,特异度 = 65.0%,阴性预测值 = 93.0%),显著优于基于树的模型。决策曲线分析证实了其在广泛风险阈值范围内的临床实用性。SHAP分析显示,较低的白细胞计数(WBC_N)、较低的淋巴细胞百分比(Lym%)以及增加的中性粒细胞形态异质性(D_Neu_SSC_CV)是最重要的预测因子,这与CHIKV感染的已知发病机制一致。结论 我们开发了一种基于CBC参数的可解释LR模型,能够有效筛查急性CHIKV感染,具有高灵敏度和阴性预测值。该模型可作为患者分诊的可靠、快速且经济的工具,特别是在等待确认性PCR检测的资源有限环境中。

title: Surgery as a Management Option for Post-Chikungunya Chronic Synovitis Presenting as a Dorsal Wrist Mass
abstract: Introduction: Chikungunya fever is a mosquito-borne viral illness that commonly causes acute febrile disease followed by persistent musculoskeletal manifestations. Localised mass-like synovial lesions of the wrist following Chikungunya infection are rarely reported. Case presentation: We report a 40-year-old female who developed a progressively enlarging dorsal wrist mass following serologically confirmed Chikungunya infection. Despite conservative treatment, she developed significant functional limitations. Imaging demonstrated inflammatory synovitis and extensor tenosynovitis. Surgical excision was performed, and histopathology confirmed chronic inflammatory synovitis. Discussion: Post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis is thought to result from persistent immune-mediated inflammation. While medical management remains first-line, surgery may be indicated in selected cases with Localised disease and functional impairment. Conclusion: This case highlights surgery as a valuable management option for Localised post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis presenting as a dorsal wrist mass.
authors: A. A. Y. S. Adikari Adikari
journal: Asian journal of Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery

Localised mass-like synovial lesions of the wrist following Chikungunya infection are rarely reported. Case presentation: We report a 40-year-old female who developed a progressively enlarging dorsal wrist mass following serologically confirmed Chikungunya infection. Despite conservative treatment, she developed significant functional limitations. Imaging demonstrated inflammatory synovitis and extensor tenosynovitis. Surgical excision was performed, and histopathology confirmed chronic inflammatory synovitis. Discussion: Post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis is thought to result from persistent immune-mediated inflammation. While medical management remains first-line, surgery may be indicated in selected cases with Localised disease and functional impairment. Conclusion: This case highlights surgery as a valuable management option for Localised post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis presenting as a dorsal wrist mass.
source_records.journal: Asian Journal of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery

abstract_zh: 简介:基孔肯雅热 是一种蚊媒病毒性疾病,通常会导致急性发热性疾病,随后出现持续的肌肉骨骼症状。基孔肯雅热感染后手腕局部肿块样滑膜病变的报道很少。病例介绍:我们报道了一名 40 岁女性,在血清学确诊的基孔肯雅热感染后出现了逐渐增大的手腕背侧肿块。尽管 治疗 比较保守,她还是出现了明显的功能限制。影像学显示炎症性滑膜炎和伸肌腱鞘炎。进行手术切除,组织病理学证实为慢性炎症性滑膜炎。讨论:基孔肯雅热后慢性滑膜炎被认为是由持续性免疫介导的炎症引起的。虽然医疗管理仍然是一线治疗,但对于某些患有局部疾病和功能障碍的病例可能需要手术治疗。结论:该病例强调手术是治疗表现为手腕背侧肿块的局限性基孔肯雅热后慢性滑膜炎的一种有价值的治疗选择。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify host factors that support Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replication in macrophages, as CHIKV infection induces acute illness and ongoing inflammatory symptoms, with macrophages believed to play significant yet not fully understood roles.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used mass spectrometry–based phosphoprotein enrichment-based proteomic analysis of CHIKV-infected RAW264.7 macrophages to characterize host cellular responses associated with CHIKV infection.
analysis.methods: The researchers performed mass spectrometry–based phosphoprotein enrichment to analyze CHIKV-infected RAW264.7 macrophages and compared the results with mock-infected cells.
analysis.main_results: Analysis of enriched phosphoproteins identified 2,096 altered proteins compared with mock-infected cells, of which 212 were differentially regulated, including 140 upregulated and 72 downregulated proteins (fold change ≥ 2, p.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that heat shock cognate 71 protein is a host factor that supports CHIKV replication in macrophages, providing novel insights into the molecular mechanisms of CHIKV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The identification of HSC71 as a host factor supporting CHIKV replication may inform the development of targeted antiviral therapies and improve understanding of CHIKV pathogenesis in macrophages.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, which may restrict the depth of interpretation, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed experimental outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify host factors that support Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replication in macrophages, as CHIKV infection is associated with acute illness and ongoing inflammatory symptoms. The researchers used mass spectrometry-based phosphoprotein enrichment to analyze CHIKV-infected RAW264.7 macrophages and compared them with mock-infected cells. The analysis revealed 2,096 altered proteins, with 212 differentially regulated, including 140 upregulated and 72 downregulated proteins. The findings suggest that heat shock cognate 71 protein is a host factor that supports CHIKV replication, offering novel insights into the molecular mechanisms of CHIKV infection. This may have implications for developing targeted antiviral therapies. However, the study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, which may restrict the depth of interpretation, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed experimental outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在确定支持 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 在巨噬细胞中复制的 宿主 因子,因为 CHIKV 感染会诱发急性疾病和持续的炎症症状,而巨噬细胞被认为发挥着重要但尚未完全了解的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用基于质谱的磷蛋白富集对 CHIKV 感染的 RAW264.7 巨噬细胞进行蛋白质组学分析,以表征与 CHIKV 感染相关的 宿主 细胞反应。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员进行了基于质谱的磷蛋白富集来分析 CHIKV 感染的 RAW264.7 巨噬细胞,并将结果与​​模拟感染的细胞进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 与模拟感染的细胞相比,对富集磷蛋白的分析发现了 2,096 个改变的蛋白质,其中 212 个蛋白质受到差异调节,包括 140 个上调蛋白质和 72 个下调蛋白质(倍数变化 ≥ 2,第 17 页)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,热休克同源 71 蛋白是一种支持 CHIKV 在巨噬细胞中复制的 宿主 因子,为 CHIKV 感染的分子机制提供了新的见解。

title: Co-Infection of Dengue, Chikungunya, and West Nile Viruses Among Suspected Febrile Patients in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen: A Retrospective Laboratory-Based Study
abstract: Arboviral infections have emerged as a significant public health challenge worldwide, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions where environmental conditions support the establishment and expansion of competent mosquito vectors (1). Among the most important mosquito-borne arboviruses affecting human populations are dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and West Nile virus (WNV), which continue to cause substantial morbidity due to their expanding geographic distribution, recurrent outbreaks, and potential for co-circulation in endemic regions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviral infections have emerged as a significant public health challenge worldwide, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions where environmental conditions support the establishment and expansion of competent mosquito vectors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective laboratory-based study investigated co-infections of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile viruses among suspected febrile patients in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen.
analysis.methods: The study utilized laboratory-based testing to identify viral infections in suspected febrile patients, focusing on the detection of dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and West Nile virus (WNV) through molecular and serological assays.
analysis.main_results: The study found that co-infections of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile viruses occurred among suspected febrile patients in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the potential for co-circulation of these arboviruses in the region, which may complicate surveillance and diagnosis efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the importance of integrated surveillance systems to detect and manage co-infections, which can have significant implications for public health strategies in endemic areas.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on laboratory data, which may limit its ability to establish causal relationships or provide real-time insights, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective laboratory-based study in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen, investigated co-infections of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile viruses among suspected febrile patients. The research highlights the growing public health challenge posed by arboviruses, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions where mosquito vectors are prevalent. The study used molecular and serological assays to detect viral infections, revealing instances of co-infection among patients. These findings suggest the potential for co-circulation of these viruses in the region, which may complicate surveillance and diagnosis. The study's retrospective nature and reliance on laboratory data limit its ability to establish causal relationships, resulting in moderate confidence in the results. The results have important implications for public health strategies, emphasizing the need for integrated surveillance systems to address the complexities of arbovirus co-infections. The evidence is based on laboratory testing and does not include detailed statistical analyses or long-term follow-up.

title: Manifestaciones clínico-dermatológicas de la chikungunya: puntos clave para el internista, lecciones del brote en Cuba
abstract: Se realizó una revisión narrativa sobre las manifestaciones clínico-dermatológicas de la fiebre chikungunya, con especial atención a los hallazgos de utilidad para el internista, a partir del brote epidémico ocurrido en Cuba durante 2025. Se consultaron artículos publicados entre 2008 y 2026 en PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO y repositorios oficiales de la OPS/OMS, priorizándose revisiones sistemáticas, guías clínicas y series de casos. La chikungunya cursó con tres fases clínicas. En la fase aguda predominaron la fiebre elevada, las poliartralgias severas simétricas y el exantema maculopapular. Se identificaron manifestaciones cutáneo-mucosas distintivas como la hiperpigmentación centrofacial, las úlceras genitales, las lesiones vesículo-ampollosas en niños y la exacerbación de dermatosis preexistentes. Hasta el 60% de los casos evoluciona a la cronicidad, caracterizada por artritis inflamatoria persistente. La integración del binomio clínico-dermatológico constituye una herramienta fundamental para el diagnóstico diferencial frente a otras arbovirosis y para la identificación de pacientes con riesgo de cronicidad articular.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a narrative review of the clinical and dermatological manifestations of chikungunya, focusing on key findings relevant to internists, based on the 2025 epidemic in Cuba. The review analyzed articles published between 2008 and 2026 from PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO, and official repositories of the WHO. The chikungunya virus was reported to progress through three clinical phases, with acute symptoms including high fever, severe symmetric polyarthritis, and maculopapular rash. Distinct cutaneous and mucosal manifestations were identified, such as centrofacial hyperpigmentation, genital ulcers, vesiculopustular lesions in children, and exacerbation of pre-existing dermatoses. The study highlights that up to 60% of cases evolve into chronicity, characterized by persistent inflammatory arthritis. The integration of clinical and dermatological features is emphasized as a critical tool for differential diagnosis and identifying patients at risk for chronic joint complications. The evidence is based on a comprehensive literature search, but the study does not provide detailed statistical analyses or experimental data, limiting the strength of the conclusions.

title: Insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti across sub-Saharan Africa: An overview and perspectives for effective arbovirus control.
abstract: Arboviruses transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, including Zika, yellow fever and especially dengue and chikungunya, represent a growing public health concern in Africa. Insecticide-based strategies remain essential for the prevention and control of arboviral outbreaks. However, insecticide resistance in Ae. aegypti is globally widespread and appears to be rising in sub-Saharan Africa. Here, we reviewed the distribution and phenotypic and molecular evidence of insecticide resistance in Ae. aegypti across sub-Saharan Africa and summarized the underlying resistance mechanisms and key knowledge gaps. Bibliographic databases were searched for studies published between January 2010 and December 2023. The review identified 40 studies from 18 of 47 countries in sub-Saharan Africa. Among adults mosquitoes, resistance to dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT) and pyrethroids was reported in multiple studies across West and Central Africa, while resistance to carbamates was also documented in several countries, comparatively fewer studies reported resistance to organophosphates. For larvae 7 of 40 studies assessed susceptibility to temephos, with potential resistance reported in only one study. Molecular investigations identified five kdr mutations including F1534C, V1016I, V410L, V1016G and S989P in 12 countries while metabolic resistance involving cytochrome P450s, carboxylesterases, glutathione S-transferases and other detoxification enzymes was reported in a smaller number of studies and countries. Overall, the evidence base remains geographically uneven and limited for several insecticide classes and resistance mechanisms. This review highlights important knowledge gaps, including the limited assessment of larvicides, emerging adulticide options, resistance intensity and Aedes-targeted vector control interventions, and underscores the need for more systematic and standardized insecticide resistance surveillance across sub-Saharan Africa.

abstract_zh: 由埃及伊蚊和白纹伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,包括寨卡病毒、黄热病,尤其是登革热和基孔肯雅热,是非洲日益严重的公共卫生问题。基于杀虫剂的策略对于预防和控制虫媒病毒 暴发 仍然至关重要。然而,白伊伊蚊对杀虫剂具有抗药性。埃及伊蚊在全球范围内广泛传播,并且似乎在撒哈拉以南非洲地区呈上升趋势。在这里,我们回顾了伊蚊抗药性的分布、表型和分子证据。撒哈拉以南非洲地区的埃及伊蚊,并总结了潜在的抵抗机制和关键知识差距。检索了书目数据库,查找 2010 年 1 月至 2023 年 12 月期间发表的研究。审查确定了来自撒哈拉以南非洲 47 个国家中的 18 个国家的 40 项研究。西非和中非的多项研究报告了成年蚊子对二氯二苯基三氯乙烷 (DDT) 和拟除虫菊酯的抗药性,而一些国家也记录了对氨基甲酸酯的抗药性,相对较少的研究报告了对有机磷酸酯的抗药性。对于幼虫,40 项研究中有 7 项评估了对替美磷的敏感性,只有一项研究报告了潜在的耐药性。分子研究在 12 个国家确定了 5 个 kdr 突变,包括 F1534C、V1016I、V410L、V1016G 和 S989P,而少数研究和国家报告了涉及细胞色素 P450、羧酸酯酶、谷胱甘肽 S-转移酶和其他解毒酶的代谢耐药性。总体而言,对于几种杀虫剂类别和抗性机制而言,证据基础在地理上仍然不均匀且有限。本综述强调了重要的知识差距,包括对杀幼虫剂的有限评估、新出现的杀成虫剂选择、抗性强度和针对伊蚊的 媒介 控制干预措施,并强调撒哈拉以南非洲地区需要更系统和标准化的杀虫剂抗性 媒介。

title: Congenital Arboviruses: A Review.
abstract: Congenital arboviruses represent a significant public health concern because of their ability to cross the placental barrier and adversely affect fetal development. In this review, we delineate the epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and diagnostic challenges associated with key congenital arboviral infections, including Zika, dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, Oropouche, and West Nile virus. While vertical transmission mechanisms vary among arboviruses, inflammation, placental disruption, and viral replication within fetal tissues are common pathological features. Early diagnosis is complicated by overlapping clinical symptoms, limited laboratory capacity in endemic areas, and cross-reactivity in serological tests for flaviviruses. In this review, we highlight the need for improved surveillance, targeted diagnostics, and preventive strategies, including vector control and maternal vaccination, to reduce the burden of congenital arboviral diseases. Understanding the maternal-fetal dynamics of arboviral infections is essential for developing effective public health interventions and mitigating long-term outcomes in affected populations.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on congenital arboviruses, specifically Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and addresses its impact on fetal development, transmission mechanisms, and clinical outcomes. The central question is to understand the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and diagnostic challenges of CHIKV-related congenital infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature on CHIKV and related congenital arboviruses. It includes epidemiological data, clinical case reports, and diagnostic studies, but does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or systematic review methodologies. The review does not specify databases or search dates, and eligibility criteria are not detailed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that vertical transmission of CHIKV can occur, leading to congenital infections with potential adverse effects on fetal development. It highlights that inflammation, placental disruption, and viral replication in fetal tissues are common pathological features across arboviruses, including CHIKV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that early diagnosis of CHIKV-related congenital infections is challenging due to overlapping clinical symptoms and limited laboratory capacity in endemic areas. Additionally, cross-reactivity in serological tests for flaviviruses complicates accurate detection. There is a lack of comprehensive data on long-term outcomes and specific maternal-fetal interactions unique to CHIKV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for improved surveillance systems, targeted diagnostic tools, and preventive strategies such as vector control and maternal vaccination to reduce the burden of congenital CHIKV infections. It also underscores the importance of understanding maternal-fetal dynamics to develop effective public health interventions.

The review calls for enhanced surveillance, improved diagnostics, and preventive measures like vector control and maternal vaccination to mitigate the burden of congenital CHIKV infections. title: A generalized lineage nomenclature for viral genomic epidemiology.
abstract: Pathogen genomics has become increasingly integrated into outbreak response, with recent virus epidemics better characterized by large numbers of viral genetic sequences. Effective international communication of viral diversity requires a scalable, adaptable nomenclature, and existing systems may not accommodate rapid sequence generation. The Pango lineage nomenclature system was designed to address these problems and has been applied to SARS-CoV-2 since early 2020. Here we generalize the underlying principles into a framework for virus surveillance. Lineages are defined as epidemiologically meaningful clusters on a phylogenetic tree, initiated from founding lineages and expanded across a phylogeny through a hierarchical system of alphanumeric sublineage names. Six years on from the inception of the Pango system, we discuss challenges and considerations for implementation. We present a Pango lineage framework for chikungunya virus, providing an alternative to the geography-based clade system and designating 21 lineages across 8 founding lineages. This generalization provides a foundation for future genomic surveillance of many viruses, including for emerging outbreaks and the surveillance of endemic pathogens.

The Pango lineage nomenclature system was designed to address these problems and has been applied to SARS-CoV-2 since early 2020. Here we generalize the underlying principles into a framework for virus surveillance. Lineages are defined as epidemiologically meaningful clusters on a phylogenetic tree, initiated from founding lineages and expanded across a phylogeny through a hierarchical system of alphanumeric sublineage names. Six years on from the inception of the Pango system, we discuss challenges and considerations for implementation. We present a Pango lineage framework for chikungunya virus, providing an alternative to the geography-based clade system and designating 21 lineages across 8 founding lineages. This generalization provides a foundation for future genomic surveillance of many viruses, including for emerging outbreaks and the surveillance of endemic pathogens.

title: Global Genomic Surveillance.
abstract: Global genomic surveillance has emerged as a foundational pillar of public health in the twenty-first century, enabling real-time tracking of pathogen evolution and informing outbreak response. This chapter examines the strategic architecture of global genomic surveillance, focusing on its application to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV). It explores the integration of genomic data with epidemiological, clinical, and environmental information within a One Health framework, while addressing critical challenges in governance, equity, and interoperability. The discussion covers the entire genomic surveillance workflow, from sample collection and sequencing to bioinformatic analysis and phylogenetic inference, and highlights the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive surveillance. By analyzing global initiatives, operational barriers, and emerging technologies, this chapter underscores the necessity of sustainable, equitable, and interoperable genomic systems to proactively address current and future infectious disease threats.

title_zh: 全球 基因组监测。
source_body_en: Global genomic surveillance has emerged as a foundational pillar of public health in the twenty-first century, enabling real-time tracking of pathogen evolution and informing outbreak response. This chapter examines the strategic architecture of global genomic surveillance, focusing on its application to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV). It explores the integration of genomic data with epidemiological, clinical, and environmental information within a One Health framework, while addressing critical challenges in governance, equity, and interoperability. The discussion covers the entire genomic surveillance workflow, from sample collection and sequencing to bioinformatic analysis and phylogenetic inference, and highlights the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive surveillance. By analyzing global initiatives, operational barriers, and emerging technologies, this chapter underscores the necessity of sustainable, equitable, and interoperable genomic systems to proactively address current and future infectious disease threats.
abstract_zh: 全球 基因组监测 已成为二十一世纪公共卫生的基本支柱,能够实时跟踪病原体 进化 并告知 暴发 应对措施。本章研究了全球 基因组监测 的战略架构,重点关注其在 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 等虫媒病毒中的应用。它探索了“同一个健康”框架内基因组数据与流行病学、临床和环境信息的整合,同时解决治理、公平性和互操作性方面的关键挑战。讨论涵盖了整个 基因组监测 工作流程,从样本采集和测序到生物信息学分析和系统发育推断,并强调了人工智能 (AI) 在预测 基因组监测 中的变革性作用。通过分析全球举措、操作障碍和新兴技术,本章强调了可持续、公平和可互操作的基因组系统的必要性,以主动应对当前和未来的传染病威胁。
