title: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Deserves Greater Regional Emphasis in Reviews of Emerging RNA Viruses: A Perspective from Southern Iraq
abstract: Dear Editor, I read with great interest the recent review by Obaid, “Emerging RNA Viruses: Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Challenges for Vaccine Development” [1]. The review offers a timely and well-organized synthesis of the structural and epidemiological features that make RNA viruses disproportionately likely to emerge as zoonotic threats, and its discussion of bunyaviruses and viral hemorrhagic fevers as a recognized category of emerging pathogens is a valuable contribution to a readership working across the biomedical and biochemical sciences. I write to suggest that a more prominent, regionally grounded example within this category would further strengthen the review's relevance to its predominantly Iraqi and Middle Eastern readership. Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), a tick-borne member of the order Bunyavirales, appears only once in the review, in a brief list of viruses relevant to a separate national research agenda, and is absent from both the dedicated case-study section covering Ebola and Chikungunya and the summary table comparing epidemiological trends, pathogenesis, and vaccine status across six major RNA viruses. Yet CCHFV has produced the largest and most sustained outbreak of a viral hemorrhagic fever in Iraq's recorded history over exactly the period during which this review was prepared [2]. Confirmed cases rose from 219 in the first half of 2022, the largest outbreak recorded in the country since 1979, to 587 laboratory-confirmed cases with 83 deaths across all of 2023, an overall case fatality rate of approximately 14% [3]. Notably, this is not a distant epidemiological statistic: Babil governorate accounted for the largest single share of national cases in the initial 2022 outbreak (39.7% of all confirmed cases nationally), and a dedicated retrospective investigation has since documented 290 confirmed cases in Babil province alone across 2022-2023, with a case fatality rate of 15.5% concentrated heavily among housewives and those with occupational animal contact [4]. This regional burden is compounded by the specific vaccine development challenges that CCHFV presents, and which align closely with the review's stated focus: no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral therapy is currently available anywhere in the world, despite the virus's wide endemic distribution across more than 30 countries in Asia, Europe, and Africa and its designation by the World Health Organization as a priority pathogen [2]. A retrospective analysis of the 2022-23 Iraqi outbreaks further identified a plausible mechanistic driver behind the recent surge, namely a reduction in preventive veterinary tick-control activities during the COVID-19 pandemic, coinciding with high Hyalomma tick infestation and seropositivity in domestic animals across southern Iraq [5]. This human-animal-environmental interface is precisely the kind of case study that could illustrate, with immediate local relevance, the review's broader arguments about the ecological and agricultural drivers of RNA virus emergence. I raise this not as a criticism of the review's scope, which necessarily could not cover every emerging RNA virus family in comparable depth, but as a constructive suggestion: given that CCHF is arguably the most consequential emerging RNA viral disease currently active in this region, and given that its case fatality rate, occupational risk pattern, and vaccine-development impasse map so directly onto the review's own framework, a dedicated paragraph or case box on CCHFV would meaningfully increase the review's value to local clinicians, veterinary public health officials, and readers across the wider Middle Eastern region for whom this is an active, ongoing concern rather than a historical example. I thank the author for a stimulating and well-referenced contribution, and I hope this perspective is useful for future work on this important topic.

I write to suggest that a more prominent, regionally grounded example within this category would further strengthen the review's relevance to its predominantly Iraqi and Middle Eastern readership. Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), a tick-borne member of the order Bunyavirales, appears only once in the review, in a brief list of viruses relevant to a separate national research agenda, and is absent from both the dedicated case-study section covering Ebola and Chikungunya and the summary table comparing epidemiological trends, pathogenesis, and vaccine status across six major RNA viruses. Yet CCHFV has produced the largest and most sustained outbreak of a viral hemorrhagic fever in Iraq's recorded history over exactly the period during which this review was prepared [2]. Confirmed cases rose from 219 in the first half of 2022, the largest outbreak recorded in the country since 1979, to 587 laboratory-confirmed cases with 83 deaths across all of 2023, an overall case fatality rate of approximately 14% [3]. Notably, this is not a distant epidemiological statistic: Babil governorate accounted for the largest single share of national cases in the initial 2022 outbreak (39.7% of all confirmed cases nationally), and a dedicated retrospective investigation has since documented 290 confirmed cases in Babil province alone across 2022-2023, with a case fatality rate of 15.5% concentrated heavily among housewives and those with occupational animal contact [4]. This regional burden is compounded by the specific vaccine development challenges that CCHFV presents, and which align closely with the review's stated focus: no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral therapy is currently available anywhere in the world, despite the virus's wide endemic distribution across more than 30 countries in Asia, Europe, and Africa and its designation by the World Health Organization as a priority pathogen [2]. A retrospective analysis of the 2022-23 Iraqi outbreaks further identified a plausible mechanistic driver behind the recent surge, namely a reduction in preventive veterinary tick-control activities during the COVID-19 pandemic, coinciding with high Hyalomma tick infestation and seropositivity in domestic animals across southern Iraq [5]. This human-animal-environmental interface is precisely the kind of case study that could illustrate, with immediate local relevance, the review's broader arguments about the ecological and agricultural drivers of RNA virus emergence. I raise this not as a criticism of the review's scope, which necessarily could not cover every emerging RNA virus family in comparable depth, but as a constructive suggestion: given that CCHF is arguably the most consequential emerging RNA viral disease currently active in this region, and given that its case fatality rate, occupational risk pattern, and vaccine-development impasse map so directly onto the review's own framework, a dedicated paragraph or case box on CCHFV would meaningfully increase the review's value to local clinicians, veterinary public health officials, and readers across the wider Middle Eastern region for whom this is an active, ongoing concern rather than a historical example. I thank the author for a stimulating and well-referenced contribution, and I hope this perspective is useful for future work on this important topic.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注新兴 RNA 病毒,特别强调了导致其成为人畜共患威胁的结构和流行病学特征。它包括对布尼亚病毒和病毒性出血热作为公认的新兴病原体类别的讨论。然而,作者建议该评论可以受益于更突出的、具有区域性的例子,例如克里米亚-刚果出血热病毒(CCHFV),以增强其与伊拉克和中东读者的相关性。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了 RNA 病毒的结构和流行病学特征,重点关注布尼亚病毒和病毒性出血热。它包括关于埃博拉和基孔肯雅热的专门案例研究部分,以及比较六种主要 RNA 病毒的流行病学趋势、发病机制 和 疫苗 状态的汇总表。作者指出,这些章节并未充分涵盖 CCHFV。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调了RNA病毒的结构和流行病学特征,这些特征使得RNA病毒更有可能成为人畜共患威胁。它还强调了 疫苗 开发这些病毒所面临的挑战。然而,作者认为,CCHFV 在伊拉克具有重要的 暴发 特征,尽管它与该地区相关且与审查框架相一致,但在审查中并未充分解决这一问题。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 尽管 CCHFV 在伊拉克具有重要意义,但该审查的案例研究部分或汇总表中并未包括 CCHFV。作者指出,这一遗漏限制了该审查对该地区当地临床医生和公共卫生官员的适用性。此外,该审查并未对 CCHFV 提出的具体 疫苗 开发挑战进行详细分析,而这些挑战与其所声明的重点相关。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 作者建议,关于 CCHFV 的专门段落或案例框将增加该评论对中东地区当地临床医生、兽医公共卫生官员和读者的价值。这将提供直接的当地相关性,并说明 RNA 病毒出现的生态和农业驱动因素,这是该评论论点的核心。

title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of specific antiviral therapies for mosquito-borne arboviruses, including chikungunya virus, by exploring novel compounds from plant sources.

title_zh: 来自茄科植物的螺甾烷皂苷抑制登革病毒复制和病毒蛋白表达,并对多种虫媒病毒具有活性。
source_body_en: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.
abstract_zh: 由蚊子传播的虫媒病毒,包括登革病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),构成了日益增长的全球健康负担,但目前针对这些感染的特定抗病毒药物疗法尚不普及。这种未满足的需求凸显了从生物相关来源(如植物来源的天然产物)中识别新型抗病毒药物化合物的重要性。本研究采用生物活性引导的方法,对八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物进行筛选,以鉴定具有抗病毒药物活性的化合物,针对Vero细胞中的DENV-2。五种提取物显著降低了病毒感染性,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在非细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。随后的分级和纯化过程分离出四种螺甾烷型甾体皂苷,其结构通过UPLC-DAD-MS和1D/2D NMR光谱法进行了表征。功能实验表明,这些化合物抑制了DENV的复制,表现为病毒RNA水平的显著降低、NS1和NS3蛋白表达的减少以及传染性病毒滴度的下降。阶段特异性分析显示,其抗病毒药物活性主要与病毒生命周期的细胞内阶段相关,这与抑制病毒复制和/或蛋白加工一致。分子对接分析支持了这些发现,预测了这些化合物与关键病毒酶的有利相互作用,特别是NS5 RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶和NS3解旋酶/蛋白酶。重要的是,分离出的化合物对ZIKV和CHIKV也表现出抗病毒药物活性,表明其对多种虫媒病毒具有交叉疗效。综上所述,这些发现将螺甾烷皂苷识别为有前景的抗病毒药物骨架,并支持其进一步开发为广谱抗病毒药物药物。

title: Molecular Cloning and Reverse Genetics.
abstract: This chapter describes a detailed molecular biology protocol for introducing specific point mutations into the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome using a reverse genetics strategy. The method utilizes an overlapping PCR-based approach to generate a mutated DNA fragment, which is then cloned into a pre-engineered CHIKV infectious clone plasmid. The protocol covers all major steps, from the initial PCRs to create the mutated insert to its digestion and ligation into the vector. It also includes procedures for bacterial transformation, colony screening via PCR and Sanger sequencing to confirm the mutation, and plasmid purification via miniprep. The document is structured with a clear introduction, a list of all required reagents and equipment, and a step-by-step methods section.

title: Exploring the Increased Risk of Vector-Borne Diseases Driven by Climate Change and Proposing Strategic Solutions to Mitigate the Impact. A Narrative Review
abstract: Since the middle of the 20th century, human activity has caused Earth's climate to change. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change projects that global temperatures will continue rising in the coming decades, leading to significant environmental and health impacts. This traditional narrative review synthesises evidence from previously published literature to determine the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases caused by climate change, their environmental factors, and solutions to address the issues. The vector-borne diseases, such as West Nile virus, malaria, dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika virus, are related to changing climatic conditions that create favorable environments for the transmission of the disease. The climatic factors include rising temperatures, drought, hurricanes, floods, changes in rainfall patterns, higher relative humidity, and shifts in wind patterns. The findings indicate that climate change not only expands the geographical distribution of vectors such as mosquitoes, ticks, and rodents, but also enhances their breeding and survival rates, leading to increased transmission risks. To mitigate these impacts, this review proposes several strategic solutions, including improved surveillance, adaptation measures, disease risk assessments, mitigation, and public health education.

title_zh: 探索气候变化导致的 媒介 传播疾病的风险增加,并提出减轻影响的战略解决方案。叙事评论
source_body_en: Since the middle of the 20th century, human activity has caused Earth's climate to change. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change projects that global temperatures will continue rising in the coming decades, leading to significant environmental and health impacts. This traditional narrative review synthesises evidence from previously published literature to determine the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases caused by climate change, their environmental factors, and solutions to address the issues. The vector-borne diseases, such as West Nile virus, malaria, dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika virus, are related to changing climatic conditions that create favorable environments for the transmission of the disease. The climatic factors include rising temperatures, drought, hurricanes, floods, changes in rainfall patterns, higher relative humidity, and shifts in wind patterns. The findings indicate that climate change not only expands the geographical distribution of vectors such as mosquitoes, ticks, and rodents, but also enhances their breeding and survival rates, leading to increased transmission risks. To mitigate these impacts, this review proposes several strategic solutions, including improved surveillance, adaptation measures, disease risk assessments, mitigation, and public health education.
abstract_zh: 20世纪中叶以来,人类活动导致地球气候发生变化。政府间气候变化专门委员会预测,未来几十年全球气温将继续上升,从而对环境和健康造成重大影响。这篇传统的叙述性评论综合了以前发表的文献中的证据,以确定由气候变化引起的 媒介 传播疾病的 媒介、其环境因素以及解决这些问题的解决方案。媒介 传播的疾病,如西尼罗河病毒、疟疾、登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒,与气候条件的变化有关,气候条件的变化为疾病的 媒介 创造了有利的环境。气候因素包括气温升高、干旱、飓风、洪水、降雨模式的变化、相对湿度升高以及风型的变化。研究结果表明,气候变化不仅扩大了蚊子、蜱虫和啮齿动物等媒介的地理分布,而且还提高了它们的繁殖和存活率,导致传播风险增加。为了减轻这些影响,本次审查提出了几种战略解决方案,包括改进的 监测、适应措施、疾病风险评估、缓解措施和公共卫生教育。

title: Screening of Antiviral Agents Against CHIKV Using Reporter Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes a disease characterized by chronic musculoskeletal inflammation for which specific antivirals are not yet available. Currently, a supportive therapy to alleviate fever and pain is used, but it does not limit viral replication or the persistence of chronic arthritis symptoms. Thus, the identification and development of new active molecules against CHIKV is urgently needed. Here, we present a cell-based methodology that enables the implementation of a rapid and cost-effective strategy for high- and medium-throughput screening (HTS) of compounds, including repurposed drugs or novel molecules. This methodology allows for the identification of novel antiviral hits with a good activity and selectivity profile against CHIKV.

title: Epitope Tagging and Coimmunoprecipitation to Identify Viral Protein Interactors.
abstract: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. Traditional AP-MS employs overexpression of viral proteins as baits to enrich host interactors. However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

abstract_zh: 亲和纯化质谱 (AP-MS) 是一种强大的蛋白质组学方法,用于剖析病毒和 宿主 之间的相互作用网络。传统的 AP-MS 采用病毒蛋白的过度表达作为诱饵来丰富 宿主 相互作用子。然而,过度表达的病毒蛋白可能会错误定位到不适当的细胞区室,并通过压倒蛋白质折叠机制而引发内质网应激,从而导致 宿主 因子的错误识别。为了克服这些限制,我们引入了一种基于直接感染表位标记的 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV/myc-E2) 的 AP-MS 策略,我们用它成功地发现了 CHIKV 细胞 储存宿主 巨噬细胞中的两个新的 抗病毒药物 因子。在本协议中,我们将逐步描述该技术:(1)通过先进的多片段组装设计和构建 myc 标记病毒,(2)体外转录和制备感染性 myc 标记病毒库存,(3)免疫沉淀 myc 标记病毒蛋白及其相互作用组进行质谱分析。该策略能够在生理相关背景下准确识别病毒相互作用因子,为未来使用标记病毒的蛋白质组学研究提供框架。

title: A Restriction-Free Cloning Approach for Molecular Engineering of Plasmids.
abstract: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.

title: The consequence of simultaneous and sequential coinfections of Aedes aegypti with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV on vector competence
abstract: Vector-borne diseases (VBD) caused by arboviruses represent a major public health threat in tropical regions. According to WHO’s Global Vector Control Response, more than 80% of the global population live in areas at risk for VBD. For instance, Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and its widespread distribution, particularly in Brazil, contributes to the occurrence of outbreaks. During these outbreaks, mosquitoes may acquire either monoinfections or coinfections, which can occur either simultaneously or sequentially, potentially influencing transmission dynamics. In this study, we investigated the effects of simultaneous coinfection with CHIKV and two DENV serotypes (DENV-1 and DENV-2) on the vector competence of Ae. aegypti and described the characteristics of infection and transmission phenotypes following different orders of sequential arbovirus acquisition. Simultaneous coinfection resulted in serotype-dependent outcomes. abstract_zh: 由虫媒病毒引起的 媒介 传播疾病 (VBD) 是热带地区的主要公共卫生威胁。根据世界卫生组织的全球 媒介 控制响应,全球 80% 以上的人口生活在有 VBD 风险的地区。例如,埃及伊蚊是登革热病毒 (DENV) 和 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 的主要 媒介,其广泛分布,特别是在巴西,导致了 暴发 的发生。在这些 暴发 期间,蚊子可能会获得单一感染或混合感染,这些感染可以同时或顺序发生,可能会影响 传播 的动态。在本研究中,我们研究了同时感染 CHIKV 和两种 DENV 血清型(DENV-1 和 DENV-2)对伊蚊 媒介 能力的影响。埃及伊蚊并描述了按顺序获得虫媒病毒的不同顺序的感染特征和 传播 表型。同时合并感染导致血清型依赖性结果。感染后 7 天 (dpi),与单一感染相比,DENV-1 感染率和病毒载量显着降低,而 DENV-2 唾液中的病毒载量增加。14 dpi 时,CHIKV+DENV-1 (CD1) 和 CHIKV+DENV-2 (CD2) 组的 CHIKV 感染率均显着降低,而 CHIKV 病毒载量仅在 CD2 组中降低。在连续感染实验中,无论 DENV 是在 CHIKV 之前还是之后获得,DENV-2 在两种连续感染场景中都表现出比 DENV-1 更低的复制水平。同样,DENV-2 显示出比 DENV-1 更低的 传播 效率,并且小鼠 传播 测定证实 DENV-2 的病毒载量降低。总体而言,我们的研究结果表明,白伊蚊中存在 CHIKV-DENV 共感染。埃及伊蚊与不同的感染和 传播 结果相关,具体取决于 DENV 血清型和感染情况。在连续暴露的蚊子中,根据虫媒病毒获得的顺序观察到不同的表型。这些结果突显了该共享 媒介 中虫媒病毒双重感染的复杂性,并强调了在评估流行环境中 媒介 能力和 传播 风险时考虑不同双重感染场景的重要性。

title: Development of a Single Thermal Cycling Multiplex RT-qPCR Assay for Rapid Arbovirus Detection
abstract: Background: The co-circulation of multiple arboviruses with similar clinical presentations poses a significant challenge for public health surveillance. This study aimed to develop and clinically validate a novel multiplex RT-qPCR assay for the simultaneous detection of five arboviruses in three reactions. Methods: A diagnostic accuracy study was conducted in Salvador, Brazil. Evaluation was performed using 254 prospective serum samples and 34 archived positive samples. The primers and probes for the assay were designed in silico, all targeting highly conserved regions of Dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), Chikungunya (CHIKV), Oropouche (OROV), and West Nile (WNV) viruses. The protocol was optimized in three reactions with a single thermal cycle, comprising a tetraplex reaction (DENV, CHIKV, ZIKV, and hRNAseP, an endogenous control) and two singleplex reactions (OROV and WNV). Results: In prospective analysis, the assay identified 45 DENV, 3 CHIKV, and 9 OROV-positive cases. Diagnostic accuracy for DENV and CHIKV was 96% (95% CI: 93.3–98.0%), successfully detecting four DENV cases missed by the reference standard. Furthermore, incorporating OROV enabled the identification of nine cases that conventional triplex protocols would have overlooked. Conclusion: This single-cycling multiplex RT-qPCR assay enhances epidemiological surveillance by expanding detection beyond traditional triplex targets to include OROV and WNV. This operational optimization reduces turnaround times and prevents the underdiagnosis of emerging arboviruses, serving as a robust diagnostic tool for endemic regions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 具有相似临床表现的多种虫媒病毒的共同循环对公共卫生提出了重大挑战 监测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在巴西萨尔瓦多进行了一项诊断准确性研究,评估了 254 份前瞻性血清样本和 34 份存档的阳性样本。
elements_zh.methods: 该检测的引物和探针是在计算机上设计的,针对登革热 (DENV)、寨卡 (ZIKV)、基孔肯雅 (CHIKV)、奥罗普切 (OROV) 和西尼罗河 (WNV) 病毒的高度保守区域。该方案在单个热循环的三个反应中进行了优化,包括一个四重反应(DENV、CHIKV、ZIKV 和 hRNAseP,内源性对照)和两个单重反应(OROV 和 WNV)。
elements_zh.main_results: 在前瞻性分析中,该检测确定了 45 例 DENV、3 例 CHIKV 和 9 例 OROV 阳性病例。DENV 和 CHIKV 的诊断准确率为 96%(95% CI:93.3-98.0%),成功检出参考标准漏检的 4 例 DENV 病例。结合 OROV 可以识别传统三重协议可能忽略的九种情况。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这种单循环多重 RT-qPCR 检测将检测范围扩展到传统三重靶标之外,包括 OROV 和 WNV,从而增强了流行病学 监测。这种操作优化缩短了周转时间,并防止对新兴虫媒病毒的诊断不足,成为流行地区的强大诊断工具。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该测定改进了 CHIKV 和其他虫媒病毒的检测,有助于 监测 和流行地区虫媒病毒疾病的管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在特定地点进行的,并且使用的样本量有限,这可能会限制普遍性。CHIKV的诊断准确性较高,但样本量较小,可能影响研究结果的稳健性。

title_zh: 开发用于快速虫媒病毒检测的单一热循环多重 RT-qPCR 检测方法
source_body_en: Background: The co-circulation of multiple arboviruses with similar clinical presentations poses a significant challenge for public health surveillance. This study aimed to develop and clinically validate a novel multiplex RT-qPCR assay for the simultaneous detection of five arboviruses in three reactions. Methods: A diagnostic accuracy study was conducted in Salvador, Brazil. Evaluation was performed using 254 prospective serum samples and 34 archived positive samples. The primers and probes for the assay were designed in silico, all targeting highly conserved regions of Dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), Chikungunya (CHIKV), Oropouche (OROV), and West Nile (WNV) viruses. The protocol was optimized in three reactions with a single thermal cycle, comprising a tetraplex reaction (DENV, CHIKV, ZIKV, and hRNAseP, an endogenous control) and two singleplex reactions (OROV and WNV). Results: In prospective analysis, the assay identified 45 DENV, 3 CHIKV, and 9 OROV-positive cases. Diagnostic accuracy for DENV and CHIKV was 96% (95% CI: 93.3–98.0%), successfully detecting four DENV cases missed by the reference standard. Furthermore, incorporating OROV enabled the identification of nine cases that conventional triplex protocols would have overlooked. Conclusion: This single-cycling multiplex RT-qPCR assay enhances epidemiological surveillance by expanding detection beyond traditional triplex targets to include OROV and WNV. This operational optimization reduces turnaround times and prevents the underdiagnosis of emerging arboviruses, serving as a robust diagnostic tool for endemic regions.
abstract_zh: 背景:具有相似临床表现的多种虫媒病毒的共同循环对公共卫生提出了重大挑战 监测。本研究旨在开发并临床验证一种新型多重 RT-qPCR 检测方法,用于在三个反应中同时检测五种虫媒病毒。方法:在巴西萨尔瓦多进行了一项诊断准确性研究。使用 254 份前瞻性血清样本和 34 份存档的阳性样本进行评估。该检测的引物和探针均通过计算机设计,均针对登革热 (DENV)、寨卡 (ZIKV)、基孔肯雅 (CHIKV)、奥罗普切 (OROV) 和西尼罗河 (WNV) 病毒的高度保守区域。该方案在单个热循环的三个反应中进行了优化,包括一个四重反应(DENV、CHIKV、ZIKV 和 hRNAseP,内源性对照)和两个单重反应(OROV 和 WNV)。结果:在前瞻性分析中,该检测确定了 45 例 DENV、3 例 CHIKV 和 9 例 OROV 阳性病例。DENV 和 CHIKV 的诊断准确率为 96%(95% CI:93.3-98.0%),成功检出参考标准漏检的 4 例 DENV 病例。此外,结合 OROV 可以识别传统三重协议可能忽略的九种情况。结论:这种单循环多重 RT-qPCR 检测通过将检测范围扩展到传统三重目标之外,包括 OROV 和 WNV,从而增强了流行病学 监测。这种操作优化缩短了周转时间,并防止对新兴虫媒病毒的诊断不足,成为流行地区的强大诊断工具。

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

title_zh: 通过流式细胞术分析虫媒病毒感染组织的细胞群。
source_body_en: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

title: Arbovirus circulation in Brazil: a scoping review protocol
abstract: Arboviruses transmitted by Aedes species—predominantly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus—represent a major public health challenge in Brazil. The co-circulation, re-emergence, and recurring epidemics of Dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), alongside the potential re-urbanization risk of Yellow Fever virus (YFV) over recent decades, have imposed severe health, social, and economic burdens across diverse geographic regions. Despite extensive epidemiological surveillance and research, literature remains fragmented regarding local variations in infection frequency, population susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, and regional disease burdens. A systematic mapping of published evidence—specifically focusing on human infection and exposure evidenced by laboratory detection methods (molecular, serological, or viral isolation)—is necessary to synthesize current knowledge, delineate spatial-temporal patterns, and identify critical evidence gaps in Aedes-borne arboviral research across Brazilian urban and peri-urban environments.

title_zh: 巴西虫媒病毒传播:范围审查协议
source_body_en: Arboviruses transmitted by Aedes species—predominantly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus—represent a major public health challenge in Brazil. The co-circulation, re-emergence, and recurring epidemics of Dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), alongside the potential re-urbanization risk of Yellow Fever virus (YFV) over recent decades, have imposed severe health, social, and economic burdens across diverse geographic regions. Despite extensive epidemiological surveillance and research, literature remains fragmented regarding local variations in infection frequency, population susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, and regional disease burdens. A systematic mapping of published evidence—specifically focusing on human infection and exposure evidenced by laboratory detection methods (molecular, serological, or viral isolation)—is necessary to synthesize current knowledge, delineate spatial-temporal patterns, and identify critical evidence gaps in Aedes-borne arboviral research across Brazilian urban and peri-urban environments.

title: Retinal manifestations of neglected tropical diseases.
abstract: Purpose of review Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) are increasingly encountered outside endemic regions due to global migration, international travel, and climate change. This review addresses the timely need for ophthalmologists to recognize the retinal manifestations of NTDs, as these conditions now appear in developed nations where clinicians may have limited prior exposure. Recent findings Modern multimodal imaging has revealed distinct retinal patterns that are frequently seen in NTDs. Dengue and chikungunya present with maculopathy, foveolitis, and retinal hemorrhages. Onchocerciasis causes progressive chorioretinal atrophy and optic nerve involvement leading to vision loss. Neurocysticercosis manifests as subretinal or intravitreal cysts with visible scolices. Schistosomiasis produces chorioretinal granulomas and neuroretinitis. Leishmaniasis presents with posterior uveitis and chorioretinal lesions. African trypanosomiasis demonstrates choroidal infiltrates and retinal vasculitis. Chagas disease shows microvasculopathy with retinal hemorrhages, while leprosy causes chronic uveitis with iris pearls and chorioretinal scarring. Summary Recognition of retinal manifestations is crucial for NTD diagnosis and management. Ophthalmologists must maintain high clinical suspicion based on travel history and systemic symptoms. Collaborative care with infectious disease specialists and utilization of appropriate diagnostic modalities facilitate optimal outcomes and prevent vision loss while addressing broader public health implications.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the retinal manifestations of chikungunya virus and other neglected tropical diseases (NTDs). It highlights the increasing prevalence of NTDs in non-endemic regions due to global migration, travel, and climate change. The review emphasizes the importance of recognizing retinal patterns associated with NTDs, particularly through modern imaging techniques. It underscores the need for ophthalmologists to maintain high clinical suspicion based on patient travel history and systemic symptoms. The review also stresses the value of collaborative care with infectious disease specialists and the use of appropriate diagnostic tools to prevent vision loss and address public health implications. However, the evidence does not report specific controversies or gaps related to chikungunya virus retinal manifestations.

title: Indigofera suffruticosa as a Source of Anti-Arboviral Phytoconstituents: Bioguided Fractionation, Isolation of 3-O-β-D-Glucosyl-β-Sitosterol, and In Vitro Evaluation Against ZIKV, CHIKV, and MAYV
abstract: Arboviruses transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, including Zika (ZIKV), Chikungunya (CHIKV), and Mayaro (MAYV) viruses, lack approved antiviral therapies. This study evaluated the cytotoxicity and antiviral activity of ethanolic extracts and fractions from stems and leaves of Indigofera suffruticosa Mill. (Fabaceae), and isolated the active principles through bioguided fractionation. Extracts were obtained by cold maceration and partitioned into chloroform, ethyl acetate, and aqueous methanol fractions. Cytotoxicity was assessed by the MTT assay in MRC-5 and Vero cells, and antiviral activity was determined in simultaneous treatment-infection assays in Vero cells. The stem ethanolic extract showed potent anti-ZIKV activity (EC50 = 29.43 ± 1.43 μg/mL; SI > 13.59). The chloroform fraction displayed broad-spectrum efficacy, with EC50 = 89.48 ± 2.70 μg/mL (ZIKV; SI > 4.47), 37.05 ± 2.26 μg/mL (CHIKV; SI > 10.80), and 42.39 ± 3.60 μg/mL (MAYV; SI > 9.44). Bioguided fractionation afforded 3-O-β-D-glucosyl-β-sitosterol, which exhibited selective anti-alphavirus activity against CHIKV (EC50 = 151.76 μM; SI = 2.02) and MAYV (EC50 = 150.35 μM; SI = 2.03), but was inactive against ZIKV, indicating that additional constituents account for the anti-flaviviral effect. Indigofera suffruticosa is a promising source of broad-spectrum anti-arboviral agents, supporting further bioassay-guided isolation and mechanistic studies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,包括寨卡病毒 (ZIKV)、基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 和马亚罗病毒 (MAYV),缺乏已获批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法。本研究旨在鉴定靛蓝中潜在的抗虫媒病毒化合物。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了靛蓝茎叶乙醇提取物和级分的细胞毒性和 抗病毒药物 活性。该研究是使用 Vero 细胞作为 宿主 在体外进行的。
elements_zh.methods: 通过 MRC-5 和 Vero 细胞中的 MTT 测定评估细胞毒性,并在 Vero 细胞中同时进行 治疗 感染测定来测定 抗病毒药物 活性。通过冷浸渍获得提取物并分配成氯仿、乙酸乙酯和甲醇水溶液级分。使用生物引导分级分离来分离活性成分。
elements_zh.main_results: 茎乙醇提取物显示出有效的抗 ZIKV 活性(EC50 = 29.43 ± 1.43 μg/mL;SI > 13.59)。氯仿馏分显示出广谱功效,EC50 = 89.48 ± 2.70 μg/mL (ZIKV;SI > 4.47)、37.05 ± 2.26 μg/mL (CHIKV;SI > 10.80) 和 42.39 ± 3.60 μg/mL (MAYV;SI > 9.44)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究确定 3-O-β-D-葡萄糖基-β-谷甾醇是一种对 CHIKV 和 MAYV 具有选择性抗甲病毒活性的化合物,但对 ZIKV 没有,这表明其他成分可能是抗黄病毒作用的原因。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 木蓝是广谱抗虫媒病毒药物的有前景的来源,支持进一步生物测定引导的分离和机制研究以实现潜在的治疗应用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外评估,研究结果并未考虑体内疗效或临床相关性。证据是温和的,因为它是基于没有人体或动物试验数据的实验室测定。

title: Microemulsion-based delivery of peppermint essential oil as a sustainable strategy for Aedes aegypti control
abstract: Background Arboviral diseases such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya remain major public health challenges worldwide. In the absence of broadly effective antiviral therapies and considering the limitations of current vaccination strategies, vector control remains the primary approach for reducing disease transmission. Essential oils have emerged as promising alternatives to synthetic insecticides because of their renewable origin, biodegradability, and multiple mechanisms of action. Nevertheless, their practical application is often limited by poor water solubility and physicochemical instability. This study investigated the chemical composition, larvicidal activity, and microemulsion-based formulation of Mentha piperita L. essential oil against Aedes aegypti larvae. Methods The chemical composition of the essential oil was determined by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Larvicidal activity against third-instar A. aegypti larvae was evaluated by determining mortality rates and the median lethal concentration (LC 50 ). A pseudoternary phase diagram was constructed to identify suitable microemulsion regions, and selected formulations were characterized according to droplet size, polydispersity index (PDI), and short-term physical stability. The larvicidal activity of the resulting microemulsions was subsequently evaluated at different essential-oil concentrations. A blank microemulsion containing the formulation components without M. piperita essential oil was also evaluated as a control. Results GC–MS analysis identified 14 compounds representing nearly 100% of the essential oil composition, with menthol (50.17%) and menthone (23.02%) as the predominant constituents. The free essential oil exhibited concentration-dependent larvicidal activity against A. aegypti , with an LC 50 of 175.7 μg/mL and complete larval mortality at 250 μg/mL. Among the tested formulations, PME-05 was selected as the most promising formulation for further development because it achieved complete larval mortality while containing only 5% peppermint essential oil and exhibited the lowest PDI (0.06 ± 0.007), indicating a highly homogeneous dispersed system. Conclusion The results support the use of microemulsion technology as a suitable delivery system for M. piperita essential oil, facilitating its dispersion and application in aqueous environments while retaining its larvicidal activity. The developed formulation represents a promising platform for the application of botanical larvicides in mosquito control. Further studies are needed to evaluate long-term physicochemical stability, residual activity, effects on non-target organisms, and performance under semi-field and field conditions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热等虫媒病毒性疾病仍然是全球重大的公共卫生挑战。在缺乏广泛有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法的情况下,并考虑到当前 疫苗接种 策略的局限性,媒介 控制仍然是减少疾病 传播 的主要方法。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究研究了胡椒薄荷精油的化学成分、杀幼虫活性和微乳液制剂对埃及伊蚊幼虫的作用。游离精油对埃及伊蚊表现出浓度依赖性杀幼虫活性,LC 50 为 175.7 μg/mL,完整幼虫 死亡率 为 250 μg/mL。
elements_zh.methods: 通过气相色谱-质谱法(GC-MS)测定精油的化学成分。构建了伪三元相图来确定合适的微乳液区域,并根据液滴尺寸、多分散指数 (PDI) 和短期物理稳定性对所选配方进行表征。
elements_zh.main_results: GC-MS 分析鉴定出 14 种化合物,几乎代表了精油成分的 100%,其中薄荷醇 (50.17%) 和薄荷酮 (23.02%) 是主要成分。在测试的配方中,PME-05被选为最有希望进一步开发的配方,因为它在仅含有5%薄荷精油的情况下实现了完整的幼虫死亡率,并且表现出最低的PDI(0.06±0.007),表明高度均匀的分散体系。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果支持使用微乳液技术作为薄荷精油的合适输送系统,促进其在水性环境中的分散和应用,同时保留其杀幼虫活性。所开发的制剂为植物杀幼虫剂在蚊子控制中的应用提供了一个有前途的平台。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于微乳液的递送系统可以提供一种可持续且有效的方法来控制埃及伊蚊,埃及伊蚊是基孔肯雅热和其他虫媒病毒的 媒介。这可以为未来环保型 媒介 控制策略的研究和开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 需要进一步的研究来评估长期理化稳定性、残留活性、对非目标生物的影响以及半田间和田间条件下的性能。证据是温和的,因为它基于实验室发现,不包括现场验证。

This study investigated the chemical composition, larvicidal activity, and microemulsion-based formulation of Mentha piperita L. essential oil against Aedes aegypti larvae. Methods The chemical composition of the essential oil was determined by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Larvicidal activity against third-instar A. aegypti larvae was evaluated by determining mortality rates and the median lethal concentration (LC 50 ). A pseudoternary phase diagram was constructed to identify suitable microemulsion regions, and selected formulations were characterized according to droplet size, polydispersity index (PDI), and short-term physical stability. The larvicidal activity of the resulting microemulsions was subsequently evaluated at different essential-oil concentrations. A blank microemulsion containing the formulation components without M. piperita essential oil was also evaluated as a control. Results GC–MS analysis identified 14 compounds representing nearly 100% of the essential oil composition, with menthol (50.17%) and menthone (23.02%) as the predominant constituents. The free essential oil exhibited concentration-dependent larvicidal activity against A. aegypti , with an LC 50 of 175.7 μg/mL and complete larval mortality at 250 μg/mL. Among the tested formulations, PME-05 was selected as the most promising formulation for further development because it achieved complete larval mortality while containing only 5% peppermint essential oil and exhibited the lowest PDI (0.06 ± 0.007), indicating a highly homogeneous dispersed system. Conclusion The results support the use of microemulsion technology as a suitable delivery system for M. piperita essential oil, facilitating its dispersion and application in aqueous environments while retaining its larvicidal activity. The developed formulation represents a promising platform for the application of botanical larvicides in mosquito control. Further studies are needed to evaluate long-term physicochemical stability, residual activity, effects on non-target organisms, and performance under semi-field and field conditions.

title: B-144 Performance of IgM ELISA and RT-PCR for Oropouche Virus diagnosis: defining the diagnostic window
abstract: Abstract Background The Oropouche virus (OROV), primarily transmitted by the bite of infected Culicoides paraensis midges, has emerged as a significant public health concern in South America due to the substantial increase in the number of cases across several countries since late 2023, including both autochthonous and imported transmission, reflecting the virus's spreading potential. Given that symptoms overlap with other arboviruses, such as dengue and chikungunya, laboratory testing is crucial for differential diagnosis. The diagnostic window varies throughout the clinical course of the disease: RT-PCR detection is most effective during the early stages, whereas IgM serology becomes more valuable in later phases. Aiming for a better understanding of disease progression, this study evaluated the relationship between days post-symptom onset (DPSO), the anti-IgM ratio (ELISA), and RT-PCR results for OROV to provide insights for diagnosis based on clinical evolution. Methods Serum samples (n=180) from patients in Espirito Santo State (Brazil) presenting symptoms consistent with arboviruses were tested. Analysis included an in-house RT-PCR targeting the S gene of OROV and by an indirect IgM ELISA (EUROIMMUN), with results expressed as ratio ( 10 days (n=18). Results Overall, 50.6% (91/180) of samples tested positive for OROV in at least one assay, of these, 14.3% (13/91) were double-positive, 46.2% (42/91) were RT-PCR positive only, and 39.6% (36/91) were IgM positive only. Total positivity was 27.2% (49/180) for RT-PCR and 30.6% (55/180) for IgM ELISA, with 6.7% (12/180) yielding borderline results. Sampling was concentrated in the 5–7 DPSO window, representing 75% (135/180) of the cohort. A shift in the detection sensitivity of each method was observed as DPSO increased. In the 10 days strata, IgM reactivity was 48% (12/25) and 44.4% (8/18), respectively, while RT-PCR positivity was 40% (10/25) and 22.2% (4/18). The higher proportion of IgM-reactive samples suggests greater clinical utility for serology in the later stages of the disease. Conclusion The findings reinforce the temporal complementarity between RT-PCR and IgM ELISA for OROV diagnosis. A significant proportion of RT-PCR positive cases remain IgM negative for up to 7 days, and vice versa, while IgM reactivity increases substantially from 8 days onwards. In clinical scenarios with a longer duration of symptoms, IgM serology provides critical diagnostic value as viral load decreases and RT-PCR sensitivity declines.

title_zh: B-144 Oropouche 病毒 诊断 的 IgM ELISA 和 RT-PCR 性能:定义诊断窗口
source_body_en: Abstract Background The Oropouche virus (OROV), primarily transmitted by the bite of infected Culicoides paraensis midges, has emerged as a significant public health concern in South America due to the substantial increase in the number of cases across several countries since late 2023, including both autochthonous and imported transmission, reflecting the virus's spreading potential. Given that symptoms overlap with other arboviruses, such as dengue and chikungunya, laboratory testing is crucial for differential diagnosis. The diagnostic window varies throughout the clinical course of the disease: RT-PCR detection is most effective during the early stages, whereas IgM serology becomes more valuable in later phases. Aiming for a better understanding of disease progression, this study evaluated the relationship between days post-symptom onset (DPSO), the anti-IgM ratio (ELISA), and RT-PCR results for OROV to provide insights for diagnosis based on clinical evolution. Methods Serum samples (n=180) from patients in Espirito Santo State (Brazil) presenting symptoms consistent with arboviruses were tested. Analysis included an in-house RT-PCR targeting the S gene of OROV and by an indirect IgM ELISA (EUROIMMUN), with results expressed as ratio ( 10 days (n=18). Results Overall, 50.6% (91/180) of samples tested positive for OROV in at least one assay, of these, 14.3% (13/91) were double-positive, 46.2% (42/91) were RT-PCR positive only, and 39.6% (36/91) were IgM positive only. Total positivity was 27.2% (49/180) for RT-PCR and 30.6% (55/180) for IgM ELISA, with 6.7% (12/180) yielding borderline results. Sampling was concentrated in the 5–7 DPSO window, representing 75% (135/180) of the cohort. A shift in the detection sensitivity of each method was observed as DPSO increased. In the 10 days strata, IgM reactivity was 48% (12/25) and 44.4% (8/18), respectively, while RT-PCR positivity was 40% (10/25) and 22.2% (4/18). The higher proportion of IgM-reactive samples suggests greater clinical utility for serology in the later stages of the disease. Conclusion The findings reinforce the temporal complementarity between RT-PCR and IgM ELISA for OROV diagnosis. A significant proportion of RT-PCR positive cases remain IgM negative for up to 7 days, and vice versa, while IgM reactivity increases substantially from 8 days onwards. In clinical scenarios with a longer duration of symptoms, IgM serology provides critical diagnostic value as viral load decreases and RT-PCR sensitivity declines.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 Oropouche病毒(OROV)主要通过感染的Culicoides paraensis蚊虫叮咬传播,由于自2023年底以来多个南美国家病例数量显著增加,包括本地和输入性传播,已成为重要的公共卫生问题,反映了该病毒的传播潜力。鉴于其症状与其他虫媒病毒(如登革热和基孔肯雅热)重叠,实验室检测对于鉴别诊断诊断至关重要。诊断窗口在整个疾病临床过程中有所不同:RT-PCR检测在早期阶段最为有效,而IgM 血清学在后期阶段更具价值。本研究旨在更好地了解疾病进展,评估OROV的检测与发病后天数(DPSO)、抗IgM比值(ELISA)和RT-PCR结果之间的关系,以提供基于临床进化的诊断见解。方法 收集了巴西埃皮里托圣托州180份患者血清样本,这些患者表现出与虫媒病毒相符的症状。分析包括针对OROV S基因的内部RT-PCR检测和间接IgM ELISA(EUROIMMUN)检测,结果以比值表示(10天,n=18)。结果 总体而言,180份样本中有50.6%(91/180)在至少一项检测中呈阳性,其中14.3%(13/91)为双阳性,46.2%(42/91)仅RT-PCR阳性,39.6%(36/91)仅IgM阳性。RT-PCR总阳性率为27.2%(49/180),IgM ELISA总阳性率为30.6%(55/180),其中6.7%(12/180)呈现临界结果。采样集中在发病后5-7天的窗口期,占样本总数的75%(135/180)。随着DPSO的增加,每种方法的检测敏感性均出现变化。在10天分组中,IgM反应率为48%(12/25)和44.4%(8/18),而RT-PCR阳性率为40%(10/25)和22.2%(4/18)。IgM反应样本比例较高,表明血清学在疾病后期具有更大的临床价值。结论 研究结果强化了RT-PCR和IgM ELISA在OROV 诊断中的时间互补性。在症状持续7天内,仍有相当比例的RT-PCR阳性病例IgM阴性,反之亦然;而从第8天开始,IgM反应显著增加。在症状持续时间较长的临床情况下,IgM 血清学提供了关键的诊断价值,因为病毒载量下降,RT-PCR的敏感性也随之降低。

title: Index
abstract: Raw macro-climatic and epidemiological time series are inherently prone to non-stationary biases and linear seasonal trends, causing spurious correlations that mask genuine environmental teleconnections. This study aimed to evaluate and measure the long-distance relationship between the global Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) and local Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) transmission dynamics in Indonesia from January 2012 to December 2023 (n = 144 months). Methodologically, a quantitative associative time-series design was employed within RStudio. Both datasets exhibited non-normal distributions (p=0.000) and raw non-stationarity via Augmented Dickey-Fuller testing (p>0.05). To eliminate mathematical bias, a first-order differencing transformation was applied, successfully achieving stationarity (p=0.0100). The Cross-Correlation Function (CCF) was then calculated across an interaction window from Lag -6 to Lag +6 months. The results revealed a highly dynamic double-peak epidemiological pattern, peaking in 2013 (15,324 cases) and 2023 (6,049 cases). While no instantaneous correlation occurred at Lag 0 (r=-0.0180), a significant, optimal positive cross-correlation emerged at Lag -6 (r=0.1246). This confirms an asymmetric teleconnection where an increase in the ONI—shifting toward an El Niño phase—preceding the current period by six months directly drives increased Chikungunya outbreaks in Indonesia, providing a vital baseline for climate-based Early Warning Systems.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用 RStudio 内的定量关联时间序列设计来评估 2012 年 1 月至 2023 年 12 月(n = 144 个月)全球海洋厄尔尼诺指数 (ONI) 与印度尼西亚当地 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 传播 动态之间的关系。
elements_zh.methods: 在方法论上,RStudio 中采用了定量关联时间序列设计。数据集表现出非正态分布和原始非平稳性,这些问题可以通过一阶差分变换来解决以实现平稳性。然后计算从滞后 -6 个月到滞后 +6 个月的交互窗口内的互相关函数 (CCF)。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果揭示了高度动态的双峰流行病学模式,峰值出现在 2013 年(15,324 例)和 2023 年(6,049 例)。在滞后 -6 (r=0.1246) 时出现了显着的最佳正互相关,证实了不对称遥相关,其中本期之前的 ONI 增加六个月直接驱动印度尼西亚基孔肯雅病 暴发 的增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证实了一种不对称的遥相关,即本期之前六个月的 ONI 增加直接导致印度尼西亚基孔肯雅热 暴发 的增加,为基于气候的早期预警系统提供了重要的基线。这一新发现表明气候指数与基孔肯雅热 传播 之间存在预测关系。

media_mentions.content: Abstract A man in his 70s from a chikungunya virus-endemic region of the Caribbean presented to a community hospital with one week of low back pain and bilateral foot pain and swelling. He was diagnosed with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia from a urinary source and treated with meropenem. The foot pain and swelling, documented as present on admission, were incompletely explained by the bacteremia or by the limited unilateral arterial disease found on duplex ultrasonography; a lumbar radicular contribution was raised on the day of admission and was never formally evaluated. Arboviral serology sent on hospital day 11 returned on hospital day 15 - the first day of recurrent fevers without an identified focus - as chikungunya virus immunoglobulin G positive with immunoglobulin M negative; a polymerase chain reaction obtained outside the viremic window was not detected. Chlamydia pneumoniae immunoglobulin G was also positive. The result was entered on the problem list as an active chikungunya infection and remained there for 11 days while a fever-of-unknown-origin workup proceeded. With non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs contraindicated by chronic kidney disease and acetaminophen withdrawn for cholestatic liver injury, corticosteroids were started for a presumed inflammatory arthropathy, and doxycycline was given as an inpatient course. Two attributions were then documented: the hospitalist who took over care in the fourth week recorded a probable post-chikungunya arthropathy; the discharge summary attributed it to prior Chlamydia pneumoniae infection. Neither attribution is established. Both rest on a single untitered immunoglobulin G that is near-universal in this patient's demographic and cannot date an infection or link it to the presenting complaint. This case is presented as an exercise in diagnostic reasoning when serology is indeterminate. The two positive immunoglobulin G results were read three ways in one admission - the chikungunya result as an active infection on the problem list, the Chlamydia pneumoniae result as an indication for antibiotics, and finally the chikungunya result as prior infection behind a post-infectious polyarthritis - and only the last reading fits the serology. The report weighs what the panel could and could not contribute and argues that a positive immunoglobulin G in this population should be read as a framing tool rather than a diagnosis. Introduction Chikungunya virus is a mosquito-borne alphavirus transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, endemic to the Caribbean, sub-Saharan Africa, and South and Southeast Asia. Following outbreak years, seroprevalence in affected populations may reach 50% or more [1-3]. Post-chikungunya chronic arthritis, a symmetric inflammatory polyarthralgia clinically indistinguishable from seronegative rheumatoid arthritis, develops in approximately 25 to 50% of infected individuals depending on cohort definition and duration of follow-up and may persist for months to years after acute infection [4-6]. Persistent viral antigen and chronic inflammation have been demonstrated in affected tissue despite a robust host immune response [7]. The serologic profile of immunoglobulin G positive with immunoglobulin M and polymerase chain reaction negative identifies prior rather than active infection: immunoglobulin G persists for years to decades, while immunoglobulin M and viral RNA are confined to the acute phase [1,2]. That principle is well established. What is less well handled in practice is the situation this report describes: an inpatient with an unrelated primary diagnosis, an unexplained musculoskeletal complaint, and two post-infectious candidates, chikungunya virus and Chlamydia pneumoniae, each supported by nothing more than a single positive immunoglobulin G, in a patient whose age and region of origin made both results probable before the blood was drawn. The report is therefore not about a diagnosis made. It is about reasoning when testing is indeterminate, about what serology can and cannot carry, about what happens to a predictable positive result once it is in the chart, and about constructing a treatment plan when a thorough workup ends without a definitive diagnosis. A PubMed search of the case report literature combining chikungunya terms with diagnostic-reasoning terms - ("chikungunya" OR "CHIKV") AND ("diagnostic reasoning" OR "clinical reasoning"), limited to case reports - returned no results when performed on August 27, 2026, and again on September 29, 2026. Case Presentation Sources of this report The patient was cared for by several physicians over a four-week admission. One author (JHF), a hospitalist, took over his care on hospital day 21 and wrote the progress notes from then until hospital day 26; the attribution of the arthropathy quoted below is his and is taken from those notes. The other physicians involved in the patient's care, including the attending physician of record, who wrote the daily notes for the first three weeks and the discharge summary, were consulted in preparing this report. The two student authors observed the case and took no part in clinical decisions. The account is drawn from the medical record, with the source of each finding stated where it matters; where the record contains no rationale for a decision, that is stated rather than reconstructed from recollection. History and examination A man in his 70s presented to a community hospital emergency department in the southeastern United States with a one-week history of low back pain and progressive bilateral foot swelling and pain, with difficulty walking because of the pain. He was from a chikungunya virus-endemic Caribbean region, where his chronic kidney disease had been followed by a nephrologist; the dates of his move to the United States and of his last travel to the region were not documented. His past medical history included hypertension, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, and a prior orthopedic procedure on the left lower extremity, the nature of which was not recorded. Home medications included gabapentin 300 mg twice daily, for which the indication was not documented. He denied fever, dysuria, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain before admission. His adult daughter, present throughout the hospitalization, supplemented the history. Admission vital signs showed sinus tachycardia (118 beats per minute), hypertension (188/88 mmHg), a temperature of 37.1°C, and oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. Weight was 104 kg (body mass index 34 kg/m2). No structured joint examination was performed at any point in the hospitalization. The emergency department template examination recorded the extremities as normal without edema; the admitting physician's history and physical examination, recorded the same afternoon, documented bilateral swelling and tenderness of the feet that did not extend up the legs, with the explicit note that the tenderness was "not focused over any particular joint" and a query of neuropathy. The vascular surgery consultation on hospital day two recorded warm, well-perfused feet with mild bilateral edema, no open wounds or discoloration, soft compartments, intact and symmetric motor and sensory function, palpable femoral, popliteal and dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, a palpable left and audible right posterior tibial signal, and capillary refill under two seconds. On history to the vascular surgeon, the patient localized the onset of pain to the lower back with radiation into both shins and feet, denied pain at rest, denied claudication, and described pain provoked by standing from sitting and continuing with walking; the review of systems was positive for back pain, paresthesias, and weakness. Nursing documentation on hospital day seven recorded 2+ pitting edema over the dorsum of both feet with non-pitting legs and a swollen left hand, the right hand being described as improved from the preceding day. Daily hospitalist examinations from hospital day two to discharge recorded bilateral lower-leg edema with normal range of motion and nothing further. Investigations Admission laboratory values are presented in Table 1: leukocytosis (white blood cell count 13.51 × 109/L) with neutrophilia (lymphocytes 9.3%, reference range 21.0-45.0%; 1.25 × 109/L, reference range 1.00-4.90 × 109/L), normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 82.5 fL), acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease (serum creatinine 2.10 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen 39 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate 33.2 mL/min/1.73 m2), mild transaminase elevation (aspartate aminotransferase 61 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 73 U/L), a raised globulin fraction (5.1 g/dL) with normal albumin (3.50 g/dL, reference range 3.50-5.20 g/dL), and a urinalysis with 3+ leukocyte esterase, 58 white cells per high-power field and 4+ bacteria without proteinuria. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (180.7 pg/mL) and lactate (1.70 mmol/L) were normal; hemoglobin A1c was 6.3%. Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis without contrast showed a distended bladder and perinephric stranding without hydronephrosis or calculus. Two blood-culture sets drawn in the emergency department showed no growth. One of the two sets drawn on hospital day two grew Klebsiella pneumoniae with an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase phenotype; urine culture grew the same organism, establishing Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia from a urinary source as the primary diagnosis. The full susceptibility panel was not available in the records reviewed for this report. Repeat blood cultures on hospital day five and surveillance cultures on hospital day 24 showed no growth (Table 2). Bilateral lower extremity arterial duplex on admission demonstrated only trace flow in the right posterior tibial artery, which the interpreting radiologist reported as possibly indicating near-occlusive stenosis; this segment is shown in Figure 1A. The anterior tibial, peroneal, and dorsalis pedis arteries were patent with triphasic waveforms, and the patent peroneal artery is shown for comparison in Figure 1B. The left lower extremity showed no evidence of significant arterial occlusive disease. Venous Doppler ultrasound of the right upper extremity on hospital day three and of the bilateral lower extremities on hospital day 10 excluded deep venous thrombosis (Figure 2). A left upper extremity venous study was ordered on the day the hand swelling was recorded; its result was not located in the records reviewed. A transthoracic echocardiogram was ordered on hospital day four for persistent tachycardia; its result was likewise not located. Between hospital days seven and 15, the patient developed a cholestatic liver injury with resolving pancreatitis - lipase peaking at 1,718 U/L (reference range: 14-79 U/L) on hospital day seven, gamma-glutamyl transferase 958 U/L (reference range: 8-61 U/L), alkaline phosphatase 771 U/L (reference range: 38-126 U/L), and total bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL (reference range: 0.20-1.20 mg/dL) by hospital days 13 to 15, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography on hospital day 14 showing minimal residual peripancreatic edema without biliary obstruction - for which pancreatic enzyme replacement and ursodiol were started. An arboviral serology panel had been sent on hospital day 11. The ordering rationale was not recorded contemporaneously. At the time it was sent, the patient was in the second week of admission, of Caribbean origin, with bilateral foot pain and swelling not explained by the primary diagnosis or by the limited arterial disease on duplex. The panel was performed at a reference laboratory, and the results were reported on hospital day 15 (Table 2): chikungunya virus immunoglobulin G 3.77 against a reference interval of 0.79 or less negative and 1.10 or greater positive, immunoglobulin M 0.30 (negative), Chlamydia pneumoniae immunoglobulin G positive, and Zika and dengue virus serology negative. The problem list that day gained the entry "Chikungunya infection, present on admission", which remained on the list until discharge. Hospital day 15 was also the first day of recurrent fevers without a clinical focus (a single fever had occurred on hospital day three, at the time of the antibiotic change). Sepsis alerts were recorded on hospital days 15, 17, 18, 23, 24 and 25; the white cell count rose to 22 to 23 × 109/L on hospital days 15 and 16, erythrocyte sedimentation rate exceeded 130 mm/h (reference range: 0.0-20.0 mm/h) and procalcitonin was 1.99 ng/mL on hospital day 15, and lymphocytes fell to 0.85 × 109/L by hospital day 20. Infectious disease consultation was obtained and a fever-of-unknown-origin workup followed: computed tomography of the chest (no pulmonary embolism; prominent subpectoral lymph nodes), magnetic resonance imaging of the brain (age-appropriate), computed tomography and computed tomographic angiography of the abdomen and pelvis (no focus of infection), histoplasma and brucella serologies, QuantiFERON-TB Gold (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany), malaria smear and antigen, and a venous blood chikungunya virus polymerase chain reaction collected on hospital day 16 and reported as not detected on hospital day 21. That collection fell well outside the viremic window in which chikungunya virus RNA is detectable, so the result was expected to be negative irrespective of prior infection status; the negative immunoglobulin M carries the interpretive weight in this profile. No focus was identified; procalcitonin had normalized by hospital day 25, and the fevers resolved the same day without a diagnosis. Differential diagnosis The bilateral lower extremity symptoms had several competing explanations. What the record documented for and against each is set out here; the weighing of the candidates is reserved for the Discussion. Dependent or Sepsis-Associated Edema For: the hand swelling on hospital day seven arose during acute kidney injury with intravenous access in place. Against: swelling and tenderness were documented as present on admission, before fluid resuscitation and before the peak inflammatory burden; the edema was confined to the feet with non-pitting legs; albumin was normal on admission, and there was no proteinuria. Lumbosacral Radiculopathy or Peripheral Neuropathy For: raised by the admitting physician on the day of admission; positional, back-originating, radiating pain provoked by standing; paresthesias and weakness on review of systems; pre-admission gabapentin. Against: does not explain the hand swelling. Lumbar spine imaging and electrodiagnostic testing were not performed, so this consideration was never formally evaluated. Peripheral Arterial Disease For: trace flow in one right-sided tibial vessel. Against: bilateral symptoms with a normal left leg; palpable pulses, warm feet, no rest pain, no claudication, pain provoked by standing as well as walking; vascular surgery found no acute limb ischemia and recommended conservative management. Crystalline Arthropathy For: age, chronic kidney disease, and the small joints of the feet as a characteristic distribution. Against: no gout on the problem list, no prior documented flare, no urate-lowering therapy, no historical uric acid elevation, no joint-focused tenderness, no erythema, no single dominant inflamed joint. Serum uric acid and diagnostic joint aspiration with crystal analysis was not performed, so crystalline arthropathy cannot be formally excluded. Septic Arthritis For: confirmed Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia. Against: bilateral distribution, no dominant or exquisitely tender joint, normal range of motion, no erythema or cellulitis. Joint aspiration was not pursued; in a bacteremic patient, this is a diagnostic limitation. Post-chikungunya Chronic Arthritis For: positive immunoglobulin G; origin in a Caribbean country that experienced a sustained chikungunya virus outbreak beginning in 2014 [3]; hand swelling on hospital day seven, hand involvement being characteristic of the syndrome and not explained by a lumbar radicular process. Against: a one-week history against the generally applied criterion of inflammatory polyarthralgia persisting beyond three months from acute infection [4,5,8]; tenderness not focused over any joint; no prolonged morning stiffness documented (the stiffness recorded by physical therapy increased with movement and was accompanied by pain localized to the left knee, the limb with the prior orthopedic procedure); the hand finding is a nursing observation rather than a joint examination, recorded on hospital day seven rather than at presentation, with an unlocated venous study. The available history could not distinguish an acute flare of undocumented chronic post-chikungunya arthropathy from a chronic seropositive state unrelated to the presentation. Post-infectious Arthropathy Attributed to Chlamydia pneumoniae For: positive immunoglobulin G. Against: no respiratory illness; a single positive immunoglobulin G in a patient in his 70s does not establish active or recent infection; no titer, no paired sera; and the evidence linking Chlamydia pneumoniae to reactive arthritis is weaker than that for Chlamydia trachomatis [9]. Recurrent Fever This was considered separately from the foot pain. Blood cultures were negative from hospital day five; there was no focus on cross-sectional imaging; broad serology was negative; the fever resolved by hospital day 25. No unifying diagnosis for the fevers was documented. Treatment Empirical ceftriaxone was initiated as part of the sepsis bundle on admission and changed to meropenem on hospital day three, when fever occurred and an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase phenotype was suspected - 1 g intravenously every 12 hours at an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 35 mL/min/1.73 m2, increased to every eight hours as renal function recovered, for a planned 14-day course. title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein
abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host-cell attachment, immune recognition, and lineage diversification. The E2 glycoprotein is a key antigenic determinant that influences viral evolution and epidemic dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories.
analysis.methods: The study applied diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on the E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, spatial–temporal stratification and analysis were performed using Fixation index test (Fst).
analysis.main_results: Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CHIKV E2 lineages, supported by codon-based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage-specific sites.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein, emphasizing its role in viral adaptation and immune evasion. These results provide novel insights into the evolutionary pressures shaping CHIKV lineages and their implications for immune recognition and epidemic dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study's results can inform surveillance strategies for CHIKV by highlighting the genetic diversity patterns and evolutionary pressures that may influence viral adaptation and immune evasion. This knowledge is crucial for understanding the potential for immune escape and developing targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on a comprehensive dataset, but the analysis of genetic diversity and evolutionary pressures is limited by the availability of sequences and the potential for geographic and temporal biases. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on existing sequence data and the absence of direct experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host-cell attachment, immune recognition, and lineage diversification. Using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods, the research applied diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotype network analysis to characterize evolutionary pressures. Results showed that nucleotide diversity was highest in the pre-expansion period (Pi = 0.085) and lower in more recent outbreaks (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests indicated both purifying and positive selection across CHIKV E2 lineages, with lineage-specific diversifying signals observed at key codons. These findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion. The study's evidence is moderate in strength due to reliance on existing sequence data and potential biases, but it provides valuable insights for understanding CHIKV evolution and informing surveillance strategies.

title_zh: 全球遗传多样性及进化在基孔肯雅病毒 E2糖蛋白中的模式
source_body_en: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.

title: A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

source_records.title: A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.
